fuentes/ley-avellaneda/titulo.texto: Ley de Inmigración y Colonización (Ley 817, “Ley Avellaneda”)

fuentes/ley-avellaneda/resumen.texto: Law enacted in 1876, during Avellaneda's presidency, that organized immigration and the colonization of public lands. It created the General Department of Immigration, offered immigrants subsidized passage, lodging and transport to the interior, and regulated the granting of plots to settlers.

fuentes/ley-avellaneda/por_que_importa.texto: It was the legal framework for the mass immigration that between 1880 and 1930 brought millions of Europeans, mostly Italians and Spaniards, and changed the makeup of the country's population.

fuentes/ley-1420/resumen.texto: Law of July 1884 that established common, compulsory, free and graded primary education for children aged 6 to 14 in the Capital, the colonies and the national territories. Religious instruction was moved outside class hours and placed in the hands of the ministers of each faith, which led to a sharp conflict with the Catholic Church.

fuentes/ley-1420/por_que_importa.texto: It was the foundation of Argentine public schooling, inspired by Sarmiento's ideas, and sustained the mass literacy of immigrants' children; it remained in force until the Federal Education Law of 1993.

fuentes/ley-de-residencia/resumen.texto: Law proposed by Miguel Cané and enacted in November 1902, in the midst of a general strike, that authorized the Executive to expel without prior trial foreigners who endangered national security or disturbed public order, and to bar their entry.

fuentes/ley-de-residencia/por_que_import.texto: It was the main legal instrument against anarchism and immigrant-led trade unionism; the labor movement demanded its repeal for half a century, until 1958.

fuentes/informe-bialet-masse/titulo.texto: Informe sobre el estado de las clases obreras argentinas

fuentes/informe-bialet-masse/resumen.texto: Report commissioned by Interior Minister Joaquín V. González from the Catalan physician and lawyer Juan Bialet Massé, who traveled the country in 1904 and described the working hours, wages, diet, housing and health of workers in each region, with particular attention to the logging camps and sugar mills of the north and the Chaco.

fuentes/informe-bialet-masse/por_que_imp.texto: It accompanied González's draft National Labor Law, which was not passed, and is a key source on working conditions in the early 20th century.

fuentes/informe-bialet-masse/leer.0.titu.texto: Scanned first volume on Internet Archive

fuentes/ley-saenz-pena/titulo.texto: Ley Sáenz Peña (Ley 8871 de elecciones nacionales)

fuentes/ley-saenz-pena/resumen.texto: Electoral law of February 1912, promoted by President Roque Sáenz Peña and his minister Indalecio Gómez, that established universal, secret and compulsory voting for male citizens based on the military register, and the incomplete-list system: two thirds of the seats for the majority and one third for the leading minority.

fuentes/ley-saenz-pena/por_que_importa.texto: It ended fraud in national elections and made possible Yrigoyen's victory in 1916; after the 1930 coup, fraud returned in the so-called Infamous Decade. Women remained excluded until the law of 1947.

fuentes/manifiesto-liminar/titulo.texto: Liminar Manifesto (“The Argentine Youth of Córdoba to the Free Men of South America”)

fuentes/manifiesto-liminar/resumen.texto: Manifesto of the University Federation of Córdoba of 21 June 1918, written by Deodoro Roca. It denounces the clerical and conservative control of the university and calls for autonomy, co-governance with student participation, competitive hiring of professors and academic freedom; it declares that “the sorrows that remain are the freedoms that are lacking”.

fuentes/manifiesto-liminar/por_que_impor.texto: It is the founding text of the University Reform, whose principles spread to universities across Latin America.

fuentes/la-hora-de-la-espada/titulo.texto: Ayacucho Speech (“The Hour of the Sword”)

fuentes/la-hora-de-la-espada/resumen.texto: Speech delivered by Lugones in Lima in December 1924, at the centenary of the battle of Ayacucho, in which he declared that “for the good of the world, the hour of the sword has struck once again” and called for military rule in the face of liberal democracy and communism.

fuentes/la-hora-de-la-espada/por_que_imp.texto: It is an ideological forerunner of the 1930 coup and of Argentine authoritarian nationalism.

fuentes/el-hombre-que-esta-solo-y-espera.texto: El hombre que está solo y espera
Essay on the average porteño, whom Scalabrini calls “the man of Corrientes and Esmeralda”: a solitary, intuitive man, distrustful of imported ideas, who awaits a collective cause to rally him.
It was a bestseller and a forerunner of the popular nationalism that Scalabrini would develop with FORJA.

fuentes/radiografia-de-la-pampa/resumen.texto: Essay that interprets Argentine history as the clash between models imported by the elites and a geographic and social reality that distorts them; the vastness of the pampa, isolation and loneliness appear as forces that shape the national character.

fuentes/radiografia-de-la-pampa/por_que_.texto: Written after the 1930 coup, it is one of the great essays of national interpretation and won the National Prize for Literature.

fuentes/pacto-roca-runciman/autor.texto: Julio Argentino Roca Jr. and Walter Runciman

fuentes/pacto-roca-runciman/resumen.texto: Agreement signed in London on 1 May 1933 by Argentine Vice President Julio A. Roca Jr. and British President of the Board of Trade Walter Runciman. The United Kingdom pledged to keep buying Argentine beef, and Argentina reserved 85% of the export quota for foreign meatpacking plants, lowered tariffs on British goods and promised favorable treatment to British companies.

fuentes/pacto-roca-runciman/por_que_impo.texto: For its defenders it protected the country's main market in the midst of the world crisis; for its critics, from Lisandro de la Torre to FORJA, it entrenched dependence on Great Britain.

fuentes/tratado-antibelico/titulo.texto: Anti-War Treaty of Non-Aggression and Conciliation (Saavedra Lamas Treaty)

fuentes/tratado-antibelico/resumen.texto: Treaty proposed by the Argentine foreign minister and signed in Rio de Janeiro on 10 October 1933 by Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Mexico, Paraguay and Uruguay, and later opened to other countries. It condemns wars of aggression, commits signatories not to recognize territorial acquisitions obtained by force and establishes conciliation procedures.

fuentes/tratado-antibelico/por_que_impor.texto: It was one of the achievements cited for Saavedra Lamas's 1936 Nobel Peace Prize, along with his mediation in the Chaco War.

fuentes/debate-de-las-carnes/titulo.texto: Speeches on the meat trade in the Senate

fuentes/debate-de-las-carnes/escrita.lug.texto: Palace of the Argentine National Congress

fuentes/debate-de-las-carnes/resumen.texto: Lisandro de la Torre's speeches in the Senate, between June and July 1935, on the investigation into the meat trade. He accused British and American meatpacking plants of evading taxes and manipulating prices to the detriment of cattle ranchers, and ministers of the Justo government of covering for them.

fuentes/debate-de-las-carnes/por_que_imp.texto: It is the best-known denunciation of the Roca–Runciman pact and the Infamous Decade; on 23 July 1935 a gunman killed Senator Enzo Bordabehere on the chamber floor.

fuentes/historia-de-los-ferrocarriles-ar.texto: Study that reconstructs the formation of the railway network and argues that its fan-shaped layout converging on the port of Buenos Aires, its rates and its state guarantees served British interests and held back the development of the interior.
It was the main intellectual argument for the nationalization of the railways in 1948; its critics noted that it underestimated the railway's contribution to agro-export expansion.

fuentes/estatuto-del-peon/resumen.texto: Decree of 1944, promoted by Perón from the Secretariat of Labor and Social Welfare, that set minimum wages, Sunday rest, paid vacations, housing and food standards and medical care for rural laborers.

fuentes/estatuto-del-peon/por_que_import.texto: It was opposed by the Sociedad Rural and the large landowners and helped win the support of rural workers for Perón; the dictatorship replaced it in 1980.

fuentes/declaracion-de-guerra-de-argenti.texto: Decree declaring war on Japan and Germany (Decree 6945/45)
Decree of 27 March 1945 by which the Farrell government declared a state of war with the Empire of Japan and with Germany, as Japan's ally, and adhered to the Act of Chapultepec.
It ended the neutrality Argentina had maintained for most of the war, under pressure from the United States, and allowed it to join the United Nations as a founding member.

fuentes/discurso-del-17-de-octubre/resum.texto: Speech that Perón delivered after eleven at night from the balcony of the Casa Rosada, following his release, before the crowd of workers that had demanded his return all day. He announced that he was leaving the Army to become an ordinary citizen, called for unity among the people, the Army and the police, and asked the demonstrators to disperse peacefully.

fuentes/discurso-del-17-de-octubre/por_q.texto: It is the founding act of Peronism; 17 October is celebrated as Loyalty Day.

fuentes/primer-plan-quinquenal/autor.texto: Secretaría Técnica de la Presidencia (José Figuerola)

fuentes/primer-plan-quinquenal/resumen.texto: Government plan presented by Perón to Congress in October 1946 and prepared by José Figuerola's Technical Secretariat. It proposed to industrialize the country, nationalize public services, expand public works, health and education, and redistribute income in favor of wage earners.

fuentes/primer-plan-quinquenal/por_que_i.texto: It was the Argentine state's first attempt at comprehensive economic planning and guided the policy of the first Peronist government.

fuentes/declaracion-de-independencia-eco.texto: Act signed by Perón on 9 July 1947 in the Casa Histórica in Tucumán, together with representatives of the productive sectors, proclaiming the will to “break the dominating bonds of foreign capitalism entrenched in the country” and to regain self-government over the nation's economic resources. It accompanied the purchase of the British railways and the cancellation of the foreign debt.
It expresses one of the three banners of Peronism, along with social justice and political sovereignty; its critics point out that it did not prevent the balance-of-payments crisis of 1949-1952.

fuentes/ley-13010/escrita.lugar.texto: Palace of the Argentine National Congress

fuentes/ley-13010/resumen.texto: Law enacted in September 1947 that granted women the same political rights as men: to vote and to be elected. Eva Perón promoted it from the speaker's platform and on the radio, and received it at a rally in the Plaza de Mayo.

fuentes/ley-13010/por_que_importa.texto: Women voted for the first time in national elections in 1951, and 23 female deputies and 6 female senators, all Peronists, entered Congress.

fuentes/doctrina-peronista/resumen.texto: Official collection of Perón's speeches and writings arranged by topic: social justice, the third position between capitalist individualism and communist collectivism, the social function of property and capital, the dignifying of labor and the organization of the people.

fuentes/doctrina-peronista/por_que_impor.texto: It was one of the first systematic bodies of Justicialist doctrine and was used to train the movement's cadres.

fuentes/la-comunidad-organizada/resumen.texto: Closing address of the First National Congress of Philosophy, read by Perón in Mendoza on 9 April 1949. It surveys philosophy from the Greeks to Hegel and Marx to propose a community in which the individual fulfills himself in harmony with society, without the selfishness of liberal individualism or the absorption of collectivism.

fuentes/la-comunidad-organizada/por_que_.texto: It is Peronism's most philosophically ambitious text; how much Perón himself wrote and how much his philosopher collaborators wrote is debated.

fuentes/constitucion-de-1949/escrita.lug.texto: Palace of the Argentine National Congress

fuentes/constitucion-de-1949/resumen.texto: Reform enacted on 11 March 1949 by a convention with a Peronist majority, with Arturo Sampay as its chief ideologue. It incorporated the rights of workers, the family, the elderly and education, the social function of property, state ownership of minerals, oil and public services (Article 40) and indefinite presidential reelection.

fuentes/constitucion-de-1949/por_que_imp.texto: For Peronism it was the expression of social constitutionalism; the opposition challenged the way it was convened and the reelection clause. The Revolución Libertadora repealed it by proclamation in 1956.

fuentes/las-veinte-verdades-peronistas/r.texto: List of twenty principles read by Perón on 17 October 1950 from the balcony of the Casa Rosada. Among them: “true democracy is one in which the government does what the people want and defends a single interest: that of the people”, “for a Peronist there can be nothing better than another Peronist” and “in the New Argentina the only privileged ones are the children”.

fuentes/las-veinte-verdades-peronistas/p.texto: It is the most widely circulated summary of Justicialist doctrine and is still quoted among Peronist activists.

fuentes/conduccion-politica/resumen.texto: Book collecting the lectures Perón gave at the Escuela Superior Peronista in 1951. It applies concepts of military command to politics: common doctrine, organization, strategy and tactics, and the role of the leader and of the intermediate cadres.

fuentes/conduccion-politica/por_que_impo.texto: It was a training manual for leaders and sets out Perón's conception of leadership and of the movement's organization.

fuentes/la-razon-de-mi-vida/resumen.texto: Autobiographical book published in 1951 under Eva Perón's name and written with the collaboration of the Spanish journalist Manuel Penella de Silva. It recounts her meeting with Perón, her social work and her view of women and workers, always in relation to the figure of the leader.

fuentes/la-razon-de-mi-vida/por_que_impo.texto: A 1952 law made it required reading in schools; it is a central piece of Peronist propaganda and identity.

fuentes/mi-mensaje/resumen.texto: Text that Eva Perón dictated in her final months, more combative in tone than My Mission in Life: it attacks the oligarchy and the ecclesiastical and military hierarchies she considered remote from the people, and defends Peronist fanaticism. An excerpt was read at a rally in 1952, but the book remained unpublished until 1987.

fuentes/mi-mensaje/por_que_importa.texto: Its authenticity was disputed for years, and relatives and biographers of Eva Perón questioned whether the text was entirely hers; it shows the most confrontational version of her thought.

fuentes/que-es-esto/resumen.texto: Essay published in 1956, after Perón's fall, that analyzes Peronism as a symptom of deep-seated ills in Argentine society. It condemns Perón as a demagogue, but also reproaches the middle and upper classes that fought him for their contempt for workers.

fuentes/que-es-esto/por_que_importa.texto: It broke with the triumphalist anti-Peronism of the Revolución Libertadora and is one of the most debated intellectual interpretations of the Peronist phenomenon.

fuentes/decreto-4161/resumen.texto: Decree of 5 March 1956 that banned the images, symbols, signs, expressions and works of Peronism, including the names of Perón and Eva Perón, the march “Los muchachos peronistas” and the terms “Peronism”, “Justicialism” and “Third Position”, with prison sentences ranging from thirty days to six years.

fuentes/decreto-4161/por_que_importa.texto: It is the symbol of the proscription of Peronism between 1955 and 1973.

fuentes/operacion-masacre/resumen.texto: Investigative report on the clandestine executions of civilians in a garbage dump in José León Suárez on the night of 9 to 10 June 1956, during the Valle uprising. Drawing on the testimony of a survivor, Walsh reconstructs the arrest and execution of a group of men, several of them uninvolved in the rebellion, and holds the head of the Buenos Aires provincial police, Desiderio Fernández Suárez, responsible.

fuentes/operacion-masacre/por_que_import.texto: Published in installments in 1957 and as a book that same year, it is a pioneering work of investigative journalism and nonfiction narrative.

fuentes/libro-negro-de-la-segunda-tirani.texto: Libro negro de la segunda tiranía

Official report of the Revolución Libertadora government with the findings of the commissions that investigated the Peronist government: corruption, torture, persecution of opponents, control of the press and the enrichment of officials. The title equates Perón with Rosas, the “first tyranny”.
It is the official document of the anti-Peronism of 1955; Peronism regards it as propaganda and its defenders as a record of abuses.

fuentes/petroleo-y-politica/resumen.texto: Book in which Frondizi, then an opposition Radical leader, recounts the history of Argentine oil and defends the state monopoly of YPF against foreign companies, criticizing the contract Perón was negotiating with Standard Oil of California.

fuentes/petroleo-y-politica/por_que_impo.texto: As president, Frondizi signed contracts with foreign oil companies contrary to what he had written, a reversal the opposition held against him.

fuentes/la-formacion-de-la-conciencia-na.texto: La formación de la conciencia nacional

Essay that studies Argentine intellectual currents since 1930 and argues that elite culture was colonial, whereas Peronism expressed the national consciousness of the masses; from a Marxist perspective, it calls on the left to join that national movement.
It was widely read by the young people who drew closer to Peronism in the 1960s and 1970s.

fuentes/correspondencia-peron-cooke/auto.texto: Juan Domingo Perón and John William Cooke

fuentes/correspondencia-peron-cooke/escr.texto: Caracas, Ciudad Trujillo, Madrid and Havana

fuentes/correspondencia-peron-cooke/resu.texto: Letters between Perón, in exile, and his delegate John William Cooke, mostly from 1956 to 1959, published in two volumes in 1973. They discuss the organization of the resistance, the pact with Frondizi, insurrection and the Cuban Revolution; in a 1956 letter Perón named Cooke as his successor in the leadership in the event of his death.

fuentes/correspondencia-peron-cooke/por_.texto: It documents Perón's strategy during the proscription and the birth of the Peronist left.

fuentes/manual-de-zonceras-argentinas/re.texto: Essay that collects the “zonceras”: ideas that, according to Jauretche, are taught as truths and serve the country's dependence. The “mother zoncera” is the opposition between civilization and barbarism, from which others derive, such as “the evil that afflicts Argentina is its vastness”.

fuentes/manual-de-zonceras-argentinas/po.texto: It is one of the most widely read books of national-popular thought; its critics read it as polemic rather than history.

fuentes/actualizacion-politica-y-doctrin.texto: Actualización política y doctrinaria para la toma del poder

Film by Fernando Solanas and Octavio Getino, shot in Madrid in 1971, consisting of a long interview with Perón on doctrine, the history of the movement, the armed “special formations” and “national socialism”. It circulated clandestinely in Argentina.
It shows the moment when Perón was encouraging the radicalized youth, before the break of 1974.

fuentes/la-patagonia-rebelde/resumen.texto: Four-volume investigation (the first titled Los vengadores de la Patagonia trágica) into the strikes of rural laborers in Santa Cruz in 1920-1921 and their suppression by the Army under Héctor Varela, with the execution of hundreds of strikers. It is based on documents, the press and survivors' testimony.

fuentes/la-patagonia-rebelde/por_que_imp.texto: It brought to light a silenced episode; Héctor Olivera's film (1974) made it widely known, and both the book and the film were banned and their author threatened by the Triple A.

fuentes/modelo-argentino/titulo.texto: Modelo argentino para el proyecto nacional

fuentes/modelo-argentino/escrita.lugar.texto: Palace of the Argentine National Congress

fuentes/modelo-argentino/resumen.texto: Text that Perón presented at the opening of the sessions of Congress on 1 May 1974, conceived as his political testament. It proposes an organized community with social democracy and the participation of organized sectors, Latin American integration, care for the environment and a council for national planning.

fuentes/modelo-argentino/por_que_importa.texto: It is the last systematic exposition of Peronist doctrine, written two months before his death.

fuentes/discurso-del-1-de-mayo-de-1974/t.texto: Speech of 1 May 1974 in the Plaza de Mayo

fuentes/discurso-del-1-de-mayo-de-1974/r.texto: Labor Day speech in which Perón, faced with Montoneros chants against his government, his wife and López Rega, called the militants of the Revolutionary Tendency “stupid people who shout” and “beardless youths” and defended the union leaders. The Montoneros columns left the square during the speech.

fuentes/discurso-del-1-de-mayo-de-1974/p.texto: It marked the public break between Perón and the Peronist left.

fuentes/acta-del-proceso/titulo.texto: Act for the National Reorganization Process

fuentes/acta-del-proceso/resumen.texto: Act of 24 March 1976 by which the Military Junta took power: it declared the mandates of the president and the governors void, dissolved Congress and the provincial legislatures, removed the Supreme Court justices and suspended political and union activity. It was accompanied by a Statute and an act of aims and objectives.

fuentes/acta-del-proceso/por_que_importa.texto: It is the founding document of the dictatorship that ruled until 1983.

fuentes/resolucion-2065/titulo.texto: United Nations General Assembly Resolution 2065 (XX), “Question of the Falkland Islands (Malvinas)”

fuentes/resolucion-2065/idioma_original.texto: Spanish, English and other official UN languages

fuentes/resolucion-2065/resumen.texto: Resolution adopted on 16 December 1965 by 94 votes in favor, none against and 14 abstentions. It recognizes the existence of a sovereignty dispute between Argentina and the United Kingdom, places it within the decolonization process and invites both governments to negotiate a peaceful solution, bearing in mind the interests of the islands' inhabitants.

fuentes/resolucion-2065/por_que_importa.texto: It is the basis of Argentina's diplomatic claim; the United Kingdom maintains that the islanders' self-determination must prevail.

fuentes/resolucion-2065/leer.0.titulo.texto: Official text in the UN Official Document System

fuentes/carta-abierta-a-la-junta-militar.texto: Open Letter from a Writer to the Military Junta

Letter dated 24 March 1977, on the first anniversary of the coup, which Walsh sent to newsrooms and foreign correspondents. It denounces fifteen thousand disappeared, ten thousand prisoners and four thousand dead, systematic torture and concentration camps, and argues that these crimes serve an economic policy he calls “planned misery”.
The day after sending it, Walsh was ambushed and killed; the letter is one of the first comprehensive assessments of state terrorism.

fuentes/resolucion-502/idioma_original.texto: Spanish, English and other official UN languages

fuentes/resolucion-502/resumen.texto: Resolution adopted on 3 April 1982, the day after the Argentine landing on the Falkland Islands (Malvinas), by ten votes in favor, one against (Panama) and four abstentions (China, Spain, Poland and the Soviet Union). It demands an immediate cessation of hostilities and the withdrawal of Argentine forces and calls on both governments to seek a diplomatic solution.

fuentes/resolucion-502/por_que_importa.texto: It gave international backing to the British military response, which the United Kingdom based on self-defense.

fuentes/resolucion-502/leer.0.titulo.texto: Official text in the UN Official Document System

fuentes/informe-rattenbach/autor.texto: Comisión de Análisis y Evaluación de las Responsabilidades en el Conflicto del Atlántico Sur

fuentes/informe-rattenbach/resumen.texto: Report by the commission of retired officers chaired by Lieutenant General Benjamín Rattenbach, created by the Junta itself after the defeat, which analyzed the decision-making and conduct of the Falklands War. It concluded that there had been serious errors in planning and in political and military leadership and recommended that the commanders responsible be tried.

fuentes/informe-rattenbach/por_que_impor.texto: It is the harshest official analysis of the war; it was kept classified until the government declassified it in 2012.

fuentes/nunca-mas/titulo.texto: Nunca más: Report of the National Commission on the Disappearance of Persons

fuentes/nunca-mas/resumen.texto: Report delivered to Alfonsín on 20 September 1984 by the commission chaired by Ernesto Sabato. It documents 8,961 disappeared persons and some 340 clandestine detention centers, describes the method of abduction, torture and disappearance, and gathers thousands of testimonies.

fuentes/nunca-mas/por_que_importa.texto: It was the evidentiary basis for the Trial of the Juntas and one of the best-selling books in Argentine history. Its original prologue, which spoke of terror “from the extreme right and the extreme left”, was criticized as the “theory of the two demons”, and a new prologue was added in 2006.

fuentes/nunca-mas/leer.0.titulo.texto: Text of the report on Wikisource

fuentes/decreto-158-83/resumen.texto: Decree of 13 December 1983, three days after Alfonsín took office, that ordered the members of the first three military juntas to be tried before the Consejo Supremo de las Fuerzas Armadas for homicide, unlawful deprivation of liberty and torture. Decree 157/83, issued the same day, ordered the criminal prosecution of the leaders of Montoneros and the ERP.

fuentes/decreto-158-83/por_que_importa.texto: It paved the way for the Trial of the Juntas, which moved to the federal appeals court when the military tribunal failed to make progress.

fuentes/sentencia-juicio-a-las-juntas/ti.texto: Judgment in Case 13/84 (Trial of the Juntas)

fuentes/sentencia-juicio-a-las-juntas/au.texto: Cámara Nacional de Apelaciones en lo Criminal y Correccional Federal de la Capital Federal

fuentes/sentencia-juicio-a-las-juntas/es.texto: Palacio de Justicia de la Nación (Tribunales)

fuentes/sentencia-juicio-a-las-juntas/re.texto: Judgment of 9 December 1985 by the Buenos Aires federal appeals court (León Arslanián, Jorge Torlasco, Ricardo Gil Lavedra, Andrés D'Alessio, Jorge Valerga Aráoz and Guillermo Ledesma). It found proven a systematic plan of abductions, torture and disappearances and sentenced Videla and Massera to life imprisonment, Viola to 17 years, Lambruschini to 8 and Agosti to 4 years and 6 months; it acquitted Graffigna, Galtieri, Anaya and Lami Dozo. The Supreme Court upheld it in December 1986, with reduced sentences for Viola and Agosti.

fuentes/sentencia-juicio-a-las-juntas/po.texto: It was the first trial of a dictatorship's leaders by a civilian court in Latin America; those convicted were pardoned by Menem in 1990.

fuentes/sentencia-juicio-a-las-juntas/le.texto: Facsimile of the Boletín de Jurisprudencia with the full judgment, on Wikimedia Commons

fuentes/discurso-de-parque-norte/resumen.texto: Speech delivered by Alfonsín on 1 December 1985 to the plenary of UCR delegates at Parque Norte. It proposes a “democratic convergence” based on an ethics of solidarity, the modernization of the state and society, and participation, in order to overcome the authoritarian political culture.

fuentes/discurso-de-parque-norte/por_que.texto: It was his attempt to give democracy a long-term program; he prepared it with a group of intellectuals known as the Grupo Esmeralda.

fuentes/plan-austral/resumen.texto: Stabilization program announced on 14 June 1985 by Economy Minister Juan Vital Sourrouille. It replaced the peso argentino with the austral at a rate of one thousand pesos per austral, froze prices, wages and utility rates, fixed the exchange rate and applied a conversion scale (desagio) to contracts.

fuentes/plan-austral/por_que_importa.texto: It drastically lowered inflation for a year, but wore down from 1987 onward and ended in the hyperinflation of 1989.

fuentes/ley-de-punto-final/escrita.lugar.texto: Palace of the Argentine National Congress

fuentes/ley-de-punto-final/resumen.texto: Law promulgated on 24 December 1986 that extinguished criminal proceedings against those accused of crimes of the dictatorship who were not summoned to testify within the following sixty days; it exempted the abduction of minors.

fuentes/ley-de-punto-final/por_que_impor.texto: It sought to close the trials and instead triggered a wave of summonses before the deadline. It was repealed in 1998 and annulled in 2003.

fuentes/ley-de-obediencia-debida/escrita.texto: Palace of the Argentine National Congress

fuentes/ley-de-obediencia-debida/resumen.texto: Law promulgated in June 1987, after the carapintada uprising of Holy Week, that presumed, without admitting proof to the contrary, that field-grade officers, company-grade officers, non-commissioned officers and enlisted personnel had acted in obedience to superior orders and were not punishable; it exempted rape, the abduction of minors and the appropriation of real estate.

fuentes/ley-de-obediencia-debida/por_que.texto: Together with Punto Final, it left most of the accused out of the trials. The Supreme Court declared it constitutional in 1987 and struck it down in 2005 with the Simón ruling.

fuentes/indultos-de-menem/resumen.texto: Decrees signed by Menem in October 1989 and December 1990 that pardoned military personnel prosecuted and convicted for crimes of the dictatorship and for the carapintada uprisings, the commanders of the Falklands War and guerrilla leaders. Those of 1990 freed Videla, Massera, Viola, Agosti and Lambruschini, as well as Firmenich.

fuentes/indultos-de-menem/por_que_import.texto: Menem presented them as national pacification; human rights organizations rejected them, and the Supreme Court declared them invalid for crimes against humanity in 2007 (Mazzeo ruling).

fuentes/ley-de-convertibilidad/escrita.l.texto: Palace of the Argentine National Congress

fuentes/ley-de-convertibilidad/resumen.texto: Law passed on 27 March 1991, drafted by Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo, that from 1 April set the parity at 10,000 australes per dollar (one peso per dollar from 1992), required the Central Bank to back the monetary base with reserves and prohibited the indexation of contracts.

fuentes/ley-de-convertibilidad/por_que_i.texto: It ended hyperinflation and brought a decade of price stability, but left the country without exchange-rate tools in the face of external crises; its abandonment in 2002 brought a devaluation and a deep crisis.

fuentes/pacto-de-olivos/titulo.texto: Pact of Olivos (Núcleo de Coincidencias Básicas)

fuentes/pacto-de-olivos/resumen.texto: Agreement signed on 14 November 1993 at the Quinta de Olivos and formalized in December as the Núcleo de Coincidencias Básicas, under which Menem and Alfonsín agreed to reform the Constitution: presidential reelection with a four-year term, a chief of cabinet, the Consejo de la Magistratura, a third senator for the minority and autonomy for the city of Buenos Aires.

fuentes/pacto-de-olivos/por_que_importa.texto: It made possible the 1994 reform and Menem's reelection; within the Radical party it was criticized as a concession.

fuentes/constitucion-de-1994/titulo.texto: Constitution of the Argentine Nation (1994 reform)

fuentes/constitucion-de-1994/resumen.texto: Reform adopted on 22 August 1994 by the convention meeting in Santa Fe and Paraná. It reduced the presidential term to four years with one immediate reelection, established direct election with a runoff, created the chief of cabinet, the Consejo de la Magistratura and the Defensor del Pueblo, granted autonomy to the city of Buenos Aires, gave constitutional rank to eleven human rights instruments and incorporated the rights of Indigenous peoples, of consumers and to a healthy environment, as well as a transitional provision on the Falkland Islands (Malvinas).

fuentes/constitucion-de-1994/por_que_imp.texto: It is the constitutional text in force, based on the Constitution of 1853.

fuentes/decreto-del-corralito/autor.texto: Government of Fernando de la Rúa (minister Domingo Cavallo)

fuentes/decreto-del-corralito/resumen.texto: Decree of 1 December 2001 that limited cash withdrawals from bank accounts to 250 pesos or dollars per week and restricted transfers abroad, in order to stop the outflow of deposits.

fuentes/decreto-del-corralito/por_que_im.texto: The “corralito” paralyzed the informal economy and set off the pot-banging protests (cacerolazos) that preceded De la Rúa's fall.

fuentes/discurso-de-asuncion-de-kirchner.texto: Inaugural address of President Néstor Kirchner
Palace of the Argentine National Congress

Speech to the Legislative Assembly on 25 May 2003. Kirchner presented himself as part of “a decimated generation”, promised to rebuild a national capitalism with an active state, to negotiate the debt without paying it with the hunger of Argentines, to renew the Supreme Court and to uphold human rights, and said he had not come to leave his convictions at the door of the Casa Rosada.
It is the founding text of Kirchnerism.

fuentes/ley-25779/titulo.texto: Law 25.779 annulling the Punto Final and Obediencia Debida laws

fuentes/ley-25779/escrita.lugar.texto: Palace of the Argentine National Congress

fuentes/ley-25779/resumen.texto: Law passed in August 2003, at the request of Néstor Kirchner's government, that declared Laws 23.492 (Punto Final) and 23.521 (Obediencia Debida) “irremediably null”.

fuentes/ley-25779/por_que_importa.texto: Together with the 2005 Simón ruling, it made it possible to reopen trials for crimes against humanity.

fuentes/fallo-simon/titulo.texto: Simón ruling (“Simón, Julio Héctor y otros s/ privación ilegítima de la libertad”)

fuentes/fallo-simon/autor.texto: Corte Suprema de Justicia de la Nación

fuentes/fallo-simon/escrita.lugar.texto: Palacio de Justicia de la Nación (Tribunales)

fuentes/fallo-simon/resumen.texto: Judgment of 14 June 2005 in the case against former police officer Julio Héctor Simón for the disappearance of José Poblete and Gertrudis Hlaczik and the appropriation of their daughter. By seven votes, with Carlos Fayt dissenting and Augusto Belluscio abstaining, the Court declared the Punto Final and Obediencia Debida laws unconstitutional and Law 25.779 valid, because they concerned crimes against humanity that are imprescriptible under international law.

fuentes/fallo-simon/por_que_importa.texto: It opened the cycle of crimes-against-humanity trials that since 2006 has led to more than a thousand convictions.

fuentes/fallo-simon/leer.0.titulo.texto: Full text of the ruling on the Ministerio Público Fiscal website

fuentes/resolucion-125/titulo.texto: Resolution 125/2008 of the Ministerio de Economía

fuentes/resolucion-125/resumen.texto: Resolution of 11 March 2008 that established sliding-scale export duties on soybeans, sunflower, wheat and corn, linked to international prices. Rural organizations responded with a strike and road blockades that lasted 129 days.

fuentes/resolucion-125/por_que_importa.texto: The Senate rejected its ratification on 17 July 2008 with the tie-breaking vote of Vice President Julio Cobos (“my vote is not positive”), and the government rescinded it.

fuentes/ley-de-estatizacion-de-las-afjp/.texto: Law 26.425 on the Sistema Integrado Previsional Argentino
Palace of the Argentine National Congress

Law of November 2008 that eliminated the private capitalization pension regime created in 1994 and transferred to ANSES the funds managed by the AFJPs, unifying the system into a single state-run pay-as-you-go scheme.
Its supporters presented it as the recovery of social security; its critics, as an appropriation of private savings to finance the state.

fuentes/ley-de-medios/titulo.texto: Ley de Servicios de Comunicación Audiovisual (Law 26.522)

fuentes/ley-de-medios/escrita.lugar.texto: Palace of the Argentine National Congress

fuentes/ley-de-medios/resumen.texto: Law passed on 10 October 2009 that replaced the dictatorship-era broadcasting law. It reserved one third of the spectrum for non-profit organizations, limited the number of licenses per operator and required those exceeding the caps to divest, which mainly affected the Grupo Clarín.

fuentes/ley-de-medios/por_que_importa.texto: For the government it democratized communication; for its critics it sought to weaken opposition media. Macri amended its central articles by decree in 2015-2016.

fuentes/ley-de-matrimonio-igualitario/es.texto: Palace of the Argentine National Congress

fuentes/ley-de-matrimonio-igualitario/re.texto: Law passed on 15 July 2010 that amended the Civil Code so that marriage has the same requirements and effects regardless of the sex of the spouses, including adoption.

fuentes/ley-de-matrimonio-igualitario/po.texto: Argentina was the first country in Latin America to recognize same-sex marriage throughout its territory; the Catholic Church, with Bergoglio as Archbishop of Buenos Aires, opposed it.

fuentes/ley-de-identidad-de-genero/escri.texto: Palace of the Argentine National Congress

fuentes/ley-de-identidad-de-genero/resum.texto: Law passed on 9 May 2012 that allows people to change the name and sex recorded on their documents through an administrative procedure, without a medical diagnosis or surgical interventions, and guarantees access to health treatments.

fuentes/ley-de-identidad-de-genero/por_q.texto: It was considered one of the broadest in the world because it does not require a psychiatric diagnosis or surgery.

fuentes/ley-de-expropiacion-de-ypf/escri.texto: Palace of the Argentine National Congress

fuentes/ley-de-expropiacion-de-ypf/resum.texto: Law of May 2012 that declared 51% of the YPF shares held by the Spanish company Repsol to be of public utility and subject to expropriation. In 2014 the state agreed to pay Repsol about 5 billion dollars in bonds.

fuentes/ley-de-expropiacion-de-ypf/por_q.texto: The manner of the expropriation gave rise in New York to a lawsuit by minority shareholders in which Judge Loretta Preska ordered Argentina in 2023 to pay about 16 billion dollars; in 2026 the Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit reversed that judgment.

fuentes/memorandum-con-iran/titulo.texto: Memorandum of Understanding between Argentina and Iran

fuentes/memorandum-con-iran/autor.texto: Héctor Timerman and Ali Akbar Salehi

fuentes/memorandum-con-iran/resumen.texto: Agreement signed on 27 January 2013 in Addis Ababa by foreign ministers Timerman and Salehi and approved by the Argentine Congress in February. It created a “truth commission” of international jurists to review the AMIA case and allowed the Argentine judge and prosecutor to question the accused Iranians in Tehran.

fuentes/memorandum-con-iran/por_que_impo.texto: Iran never ratified it, and the federal appeals court declared it unconstitutional in 2014. It was the basis of Nisman's cover-up complaint.

fuentes/fallo-clarin/titulo.texto: Supreme Court ruling in the case “Grupo Clarín y otros c/ Poder Ejecutivo Nacional y otro”

fuentes/fallo-clarin/autor.texto: Corte Suprema de Justicia de la Nación

fuentes/fallo-clarin/escrita.lugar.texto: Palacio de Justicia de la Nación (Tribunales)

fuentes/fallo-clarin/resumen.texto: Judgment of 29 October 2013 that declared constitutional the articles of the Ley de Servicios de Comunicación Audiovisual on license limits and divestment challenged by the Grupo Clarín. The decision was by majority, with partial dissents and a full dissent by Carlos Fayt.

fuentes/fallo-clarin/por_que_importa.texto: It obliged the group to comply with the law; the divestment was never completed and Macri's decrees of 2015-2016 rendered it void.

fuentes/denuncia-de-nisman/titulo.texto: Prosecutor Alberto Nisman's complaint alleging a cover-up of the AMIA bombing

fuentes/denuncia-de-nisman/resumen.texto: Complaint of some three hundred pages filed on 14 January 2015 against President Cristina Kirchner, Foreign Minister Timerman and others, whom he accused of organizing a plan to shield the Iranians accused of the AMIA bombing through the Memorandum, in exchange for trade in grain and oil. Nisman was due to present it to Congress on 19 January and was found dead the night before.

fuentes/denuncia-de-nisman/por_que_impor.texto: Judge Daniel Rafecas dismissed it in February 2015 on the grounds that no crime had been committed; reopened in 2016, it gave rise to the Memorandum case, which ended in a dismissal in 2021 that the Court of Cassation overturned in 2023.

fuentes/sentencia-megacausa-esma/titulo.texto: Judgment in the ESMA mega-trial (unified ESMA case)

fuentes/sentencia-megacausa-esma/autor.texto: Tribunal Oral en lo Criminal Federal n.º 5

fuentes/sentencia-megacausa-esma/resumen.texto: Judgment of 29 November 2017, after five years of trial for the crimes against 789 victims at the ESMA. It sentenced 29 defendants to life imprisonment, among them Alfredo Astiz and Jorge “el Tigre” Acosta, and 19 others to sentences of between 8 and 25 years, and acquitted 6; the “death flights” were tried for the first time.

fuentes/sentencia-megacausa-esma/por_que.texto: It was the largest trial in Argentine judicial history by number of victims and defendants.

fuentes/anticuerpos-monoclonales-kohler-.texto: Continuous cultures of fused cells secreting antibody of predefined specificity

Article by Georges Köhler and César Milstein published in Nature on 7 August 1975. It describes the fusion of lymphocytes from immunized mice with myeloma cells to obtain hybridomas, cell lines that reproduce indefinitely and produce a single antibody of known specificity.
It is the basis of monoclonal antibodies, used in diagnosis, research and treatments for cancer and other diseases; the authors did not patent the technique.

fuentes/favaloro-1968/titulo.texto: Saphenous vein autograft replacement of severe segmental coronary artery occlusion: operative technique

fuentes/favaloro-1968/soporte.texto: Scientific article (The Annals of Thoracic Surgery)

fuentes/favaloro-1968/resumen.texto: Article in which Favaloro describes the technique he had been applying since May 1967 at the Cleveland Clinic: replacing the obstructed segment of a coronary artery with a segment of the patient's own saphenous vein, connected to the aorta.

fuentes/favaloro-1968/por_que_importa.texto: It drove the spread of coronary artery bypass surgery, one of the most commonly performed operations in the world.

fuentes/el-camino-del-libertario/resumen.texto: Milei's 2022 book combining autobiography and program: it defends the ideas of the Austrian school of economics, presents him as an anarcho-capitalist in philosophy and a minarchist in practice, attacks the “political caste” and proposes phased reforms to reduce public spending, open the economy and eliminate the Central Bank.

fuentes/el-camino-del-libertario/por_que.texto: It sets out the program with which Milei reached the presidency the following year.

fuentes/dnu-70-2023/titulo.texto: Decree of Necessity and Urgency 70/2023 (“Bases para la Reconstrucción de la Economía Argentina”)

fuentes/dnu-70-2023/resumen.texto: Decree of 20 December 2023 that repealed or amended hundreds of regulations: the rental law, the supply law, the shelf law and promotion regimes; it enabled the conversion of state-owned companies into corporations (sociedades anónimas) so they could be privatized and reformed labor legislation.

fuentes/dnu-70-2023/por_que_importa.texto: It was Milei's first major deregulatory measure. The labor courts suspended its labor chapter and the Senate rejected it in March 2024, but it remained in force because the Chamber of Deputies did not reject it.

fuentes/dnu-70-2023/leer.0.titulo.texto: Text on the official legislation portal

fuentes/discurso-de-davos-2024/titulo.texto: Javier Milei's speech at the World Economic Forum in Davos

fuentes/discurso-de-davos-2024/resumen.texto: Speech of 17 January 2024 in which Milei asserted that “the West is in danger” because its leaders had abandoned freedom for variants of collectivism. He defended free-enterprise capitalism as the only system capable of ending poverty and criticized social justice, radical feminism and the environmental agenda.

fuentes/discurso-de-davos-2024/por_que_i.texto: It projected him as an international figure of the new right; his critics read it as an attack on social and environmental consensuses.

fuentes/discurso-de-davos-2024/leer.0.ti.texto: Stenographic transcript on the Casa Rosada website

fuentes/ley-bases/titulo.texto: Ley de Bases y Puntos de Partida para la Libertad de los Argentinos (Law 27.742)

fuentes/ley-bases/escrita.lugar.texto: Palace of the Argentine National Congress

fuentes/ley-bases/resumen.texto: Law passed on 27 June 2024, after a first bill failed in February and following its approval in the Senate with Vice President Villarruel's tie-breaking vote. It declared a public emergency and delegated powers to the executive for one year, authorized the privatization of several state-owned companies, created the Régimen de Incentivo para Grandes Inversiones (RIGI) and reformed labor and public employment rules.

fuentes/ley-bases/por_que_importa.texto: It was the first major law of Milei's government, passed with a minority bloc of its own; the Senate session of 12 June took place amid a street protest that ended with injuries and arrests.

fuentes/ley-bases/leer.0.titulo.texto: Text on the official legislation portal

fuentes/ley-ive/titulo.texto: Ley de Interrupción Voluntaria del Embarazo (Ley 27.610)

fuentes/ley-ive/escrita.lugar.texto: Palace of the Argentine National Congress

fuentes/ley-ive/resumen.texto: Law passed by the Senate on December 30, 2020, that legalized voluntary abortion up to the 14th week of gestation and afterwards kept the grounds of rape and of risk to the life or health of the pregnant person; it allows conscientious objection by health professionals.

fuentes/ley-ive/por_que_importa.texto: It came after the Senate's rejection in 2018 and the green-scarf mobilizations; groups that describe themselves as pro-life, with the light-blue scarf, and the Catholic Church opposed it.

fuentes/procesamiento-cuadernos/titulo.texto: Indictment order in the Notebooks case

fuentes/procesamiento-cuadernos/resumen.texto: Ruling of September 17, 2018, by judge Claudio Bonadio that indicted Cristina Kirchner, with pretrial detention, as head of a criminal association that allegedly collected bribes from public works contractors between 2003 and 2015, based on the notes of the driver Oscar Centeno and the statements of dozens of cooperating defendants. The Cámara Federal upheld it with modifications on December 20, 2018, and the oral trial before the Tribunal Oral Federal 7 began on November 6, 2025.

fuentes/procesamiento-cuadernos/por_que_.texto: It is the corruption case with the most defendants in Argentine history. Kirchner's defense argues that the notebooks were tampered with and that the confessions were obtained under pressure; a 2025 expert examination attributed the handwriting to Centeno and recorded hundreds of corrections made by other hands.

fuentes/fallo-ciccone/autor.texto: Tribunal Oral en lo Criminal Federal n.º 4

fuentes/fallo-ciccone/resumen.texto: Ruling of August 7, 2018, that sentenced Amado Boudou to five years and ten months in prison and a lifetime ban from public office for passive bribery and conduct incompatible with public office, for having secretly taken control, while minister of Economy, of the printing company Ciccone Calcográfica to obtain banknote printing contracts. Chamber IV of the Cámara de Casación upheld it in July 2019, and the Supreme Court rejected the last appeal in December 2020.

fuentes/fallo-ciccone/por_que_importa.texto: It was the first final conviction of a former vice president; Boudou denounced political persecution.

fuentes/fallo-once/autor.texto: Tribunales Orales en lo Criminal Federal n.º 2 y n.º 4

fuentes/fallo-once/resumen.texto: On December 29, 2015, the Tribunal Oral Federal 2 convicted, for the crash of February 22, 2012, executives of the concession company TBA, among them Claudio Cirigliano, the former secretaries of Transport Ricardo Jaime and Juan Pablo Schiavi, and the train driver. On October 10, 2018, the Tribunal Oral Federal 4 sentenced former minister Julio De Vido to five years and eight months in prison for fraudulent administration, for failing to oversee the concession company; the Cámara de Casación upheld it in December 2020 and the Supreme Court made it final in November 2025.

fuentes/fallo-once/por_que_importa.texto: It is the main conviction for political responsibility in a tragedy that occurred under Kirchnerism; De Vido maintained that he was innocent.

fuentes/fallo-jose-lopez/titulo.texto: Ruling in the José López bags case

fuentes/fallo-jose-lopez/autor.texto: Tribunal Oral en lo Criminal Federal n.º 1

fuentes/fallo-jose-lopez/resumen.texto: Ruling of June 12, 2019, that sentenced former secretary of Public Works José López to six years in prison and a lifetime ban from public office for illicit enrichment, for the nearly nine million dollars he tried to hide in a convent in General Rodríguez in June 2016. In 2025 his sentences in this case, in the weapons possession case and in the Vialidad case were combined into thirteen years.

fuentes/fallo-jose-lopez/por_que_importa.texto: The image of the bags thrown over the convent wall became a symbol of corruption in public works.

fuentes/fallo-ruta-del-dinero-k/titulo.texto: Ruling in the “Ruta del dinero K” case

fuentes/fallo-ruta-del-dinero-k/autor.texto: Tribunal Oral en lo Criminal Federal n.º 4

fuentes/fallo-ruta-del-dinero-k/resumen.texto: Ruling of February 24, 2021, that sentenced Lázaro Báez to twelve years in prison for aggravated money laundering, for having taken out of the country and brought back tens of millions of dollars, and also convicted his children, his accountant, his lawyer and other defendants, among them Leonardo Fariña. The Cámara de Casación upheld it on February 28, 2023, and reduced Báez's sentence to ten years.

fuentes/fallo-ruta-del-dinero-k/por_que_.texto: It was the first major money laundering trial linked to public works in Santa Cruz; the case originated in a 2013 television program.

fuentes/sobreseimiento-memorandum/titulo.texto: Dismissal in the Memorandum with Iran case

fuentes/sobreseimiento-memorandum/autor.texto: Tribunal Oral en lo Criminal Federal n.º 8

fuentes/sobreseimiento-memorandum/resume.texto: Ruling of October 7, 2021, by judges Gabriela López Iñiguez, José Michilini and Daniel Obligado that dismissed the charges against Cristina Kirchner and the other defendants over Nisman's complaint on the grounds that no crime had been committed, before trial: it held that the Memorandum, “whether it is considered a political success or a political mistake, did not constitute a crime.”

fuentes/sobreseimiento-memorandum/por_qu.texto: It was one of the rulings favorable to Kirchner; the DAIA and relatives of AMIA victims appealed it.

fuentes/sobreseimiento-hotesur/titulo.texto: Dismissal in the Hotesur-Los Sauces case

fuentes/sobreseimiento-hotesur/autor.texto: Tribunal Oral en lo Criminal Federal n.º 5

fuentes/sobreseimiento-hotesur/resumen.texto: Ruling of November 2021 that dismissed the charges against Cristina Kirchner, her children Máximo and Florencia, and the other defendants in the cases of money laundering through the rental of family hotels and properties to companies of Lázaro Báez and Cristóbal López, before trial, on the grounds that the acts did not constitute a crime.

fuentes/sobreseimiento-hotesur/por_que_i.texto: It was another of the rulings favorable to Kirchner, overturned by the Cámara de Casación in 2023.

fuentes/casacion-hotesur-memorandum/titu.texto: Reversal of the dismissals in the Hotesur-Los Sauces and Memorandum cases

fuentes/casacion-hotesur-memorandum/auto.texto: Cámara Federal de Casación Penal, Sala I

fuentes/casacion-hotesur-memorandum/resu.texto: Rulings of September 2023 in which Chamber I of the Cámara Federal de Casación Penal reversed the 2021 dismissals and ordered Cristina Kirchner and the other defendants to stand oral trial in both cases. On December 5, 2024, the Supreme Court rejected Kirchner's appeals in the Memorandum case.

fuentes/casacion-hotesur-memorandum/por_.texto: It reopened two of the main cases against Kirchner, which are awaiting oral trial; her defense argues that acts that are not crimes are being tried.

fuentes/fallo-dolar-futuro/autor.texto: Cámara Federal de Casación Penal, Sala I

fuentes/fallo-dolar-futuro/resumen.texto: Ruling of April 13, 2021, that dismissed the charges against Cristina Kirchner, former minister Axel Kicillof, former Central Bank president Alejandro Vanoli and the other defendants in the case opened by Bonadio over the sale of dollar futures contracts in 2015. The court concluded that it was an economic policy decision that could not be subject to criminal review.

fuentes/fallo-dolar-futuro/por_que_impor.texto: It is the main ruling favorable to Kirchner among the cases opened after 2015; her defense presented it as proof that the case should never have existed, and in 2022 the prosecutor general Eduardo Casal asked the Supreme Court to reopen it.

fuentes/fallo-milagro-sala/titulo.texto: Ruling in the “Pibes Villeros” case against Milagro Sala

fuentes/fallo-milagro-sala/autor.texto: Tribunal en lo Criminal n.º 3 de Jujuy

fuentes/fallo-milagro-sala/resumen.texto: Ruling of January 2019 that sentenced Milagro Sala to thirteen years in prison as head of a criminal association and for fraud against the public administration and extortion, over the diversion of some sixty million pesos intended for social housing through the Pibes Villeros cooperative. The Supreme Court upheld it in December 2022, and in May 2025 it made final the combined fifteen-year sentence for this and another case.

fuentes/fallo-milagro-sala/por_que_impor.texto: Sala and human rights organizations maintain that she is a political prisoner of former governor Gerardo Morales; in 2016 a UN working group described her detention as arbitrary, and she is serving her sentence under house arrest.

fuentes/fallo-vialidad/autor.texto: Tribunal Oral en lo Criminal Federal n.º 2

fuentes/fallo-vialidad/resumen.texto: Ruling of December 6, 2022 (judges Jorge Gorini, Rodrigo Giménez Uriburu and Andrés Basso) that sentenced Cristina Kirchner to six years in prison and a lifetime ban from public office for fraudulent administration to the detriment of the public administration, for steering 51 road works in Santa Cruz to Lázaro Báez's companies between 2003 and 2015. It acquitted her of criminal association, with Basso dissenting, and also convicted Báez, José López and other officials.

fuentes/fallo-vialidad/por_que_importa.texto: It was the first conviction of a sitting vice president; Kirchner attributed it to “lawfare” and denounced that the court and the prosecutors were acting against her for political reasons.

fuentes/fallo-vialidad-casacion/titulo.texto: Ruling of the Cámara de Casación in the Vialidad case

fuentes/fallo-vialidad-casacion/autor.texto: Cámara Federal de Casación Penal, Sala IV

fuentes/fallo-vialidad-casacion/resumen.texto: Ruling of November 13, 2024, by judges Gustavo Hornos, Mariano Borinsky and Diego Barroetaveña that upheld Cristina Kirchner's sentence of six years in prison and a lifetime ban from public office for fraudulent administration and rejected the prosecution's appeal to add the crime of criminal association.

fuentes/fallo-vialidad-casacion/por_que_.texto: It left the case in the hands of the Supreme Court; Kirchner again denounced judicial persecution.

fuentes/fallo-vialidad-corte/titulo.texto: Supreme Court ruling in the Vialidad case

fuentes/fallo-vialidad-corte/autor.texto: Corte Suprema de Justicia de la Nación

fuentes/fallo-vialidad-corte/escrita.lug.texto: Palacio de Justicia de la Nación (Tribunales)

fuentes/fallo-vialidad-corte/resumen.texto: Ruling of June 10, 2025, in which justices Horacio Rosatti, Carlos Rosenkrantz and Ricardo Lorenzetti rejected the defense appeals and made final Cristina Kirchner's sentence of six years in prison and a lifetime ban from public office. Days later the Tribunal Oral Federal 2 granted her house arrest in her apartment on San José street, in Buenos Aires, with an electronic ankle monitor.

fuentes/fallo-vialidad-corte/por_que_imp.texto: The ban prevented her from running in the 2025 elections; Kirchnerism called it a proscription and mobilized in her support, while her critics saw it as the conclusion of a process that went through every instance.

fuentes/sentencia-intento-de-asesinato-d.texto: Ruling in the trial for the attempted assassination of Cristina Kirchner
Tribunal Oral en lo Criminal Federal n.º 6

Ruling of October 8, 2025, after a trial that began in June 2024, that sentenced Fernando Sabag Montiel to ten years in prison for the aggravated attempted homicide of Cristina Kirchner on September 1, 2022, and convicted his partner, Brenda Uliarte, as a necessary accomplice; Nicolás Carrizo was acquitted.
It closed the first judicial stage of the case; Kirchner's legal team maintains that there were instigators and financiers whom the investigation did not reach.

fuentes/censo-1869/titulo.texto: First Census of the Argentine Republic (1869)

fuentes/censo-1869/autor.texto: Superintendencia del Censo (Diego G. de la Fuente)

fuentes/censo-1869/resumen.texto: First national census, taken from September 15 to 18, 1869, under the presidency of Sarmiento. It counted 1,737,076 inhabitants, which together with estimates of uncounted Indigenous people and of Argentines abroad totaled 1,877,490; the population was mostly rural and foreigners made up about 12%.

fuentes/censo-1869/por_que_importa.texto: It is the first measurement of the country's population and the starting point of the series that shows the impact of immigration.

fuentes/censo-1869/leer.0.titulo.texto: Census schedules for the province and city of Buenos Aires on Internet Archive

fuentes/censo-1895/titulo.texto: Second Census of the Argentine Republic (1895)

fuentes/censo-1895/resumen.texto: Second national census, taken on May 10, 1895. It recorded 4,044,911 inhabitants, more than double the 1869 figure; about a quarter of the population was foreign-born, mostly Italian and Spanish.

fuentes/censo-1895/por_que_importa.texto: It measures the first great surge of mass immigration and the agricultural expansion of the Pampas.

fuentes/censo-1914/resumen.texto: Third national census, taken on June 1, 1914. It recorded 7,885,237 inhabitants, 30% of whom had been born abroad, the highest proportion in the country's history; in the city of Buenos Aires foreigners were close to half the population.

fuentes/censo-1914/por_que_importa.texto: It is the statistical snapshot of Argentina during mass immigration, on the eve of the First World War.

fuentes/censo-1947/titulo.texto: Fourth General Census of the Nation (1947)

fuentes/censo-1947/resumen.texto: Fourth national census, taken in 1947 during Perón's first government, thirty-three years after the previous one. It recorded 15,893,827 inhabitants; the proportion of foreigners had fallen to about 15% and most of the population was already urban.

fuentes/censo-1947/por_que_importa.texto: It shows the end of mass immigration and the beginning of internal migration toward Greater Buenos Aires.

fuentes/censo-1960/autor.texto: Dirección Nacional de Estadística y Censos

fuentes/censo-1960/resumen.texto: Fifth national census, taken in 1960 during the presidency of Frondizi. It recorded 20,013,793 inhabitants and confirmed the concentration of the population in Greater Buenos Aires.

fuentes/censo-1960/por_que_importa.texto: It begins the series of decennial censuses that has continued, with exceptions, to the present.

fuentes/censo-1970/titulo.texto: National Census of Population, Families and Housing (1970)

fuentes/censo-1970/autor.texto: Instituto Nacional de Estadística y Censos

fuentes/censo-1970/resumen.texto: Sixth national census, the first by INDEC, taken in 1970 under the dictatorship of the Argentine Revolution. It recorded 23,364,431 inhabitants.

fuentes/censo-1970/por_que_importa.texto: It measures the Argentine population before the political violence and emigration of the 1970s.

fuentes/censo-1980/autor.texto: Instituto Nacional de Estadística y Censos

fuentes/censo-1980/resumen.texto: Seventh national census, taken on October 22, 1980, under Videla's dictatorship. It recorded 27,949,480 inhabitants.

fuentes/censo-1980/por_que_importa.texto: It is the measurement of the population during the last dictatorship.

fuentes/censo-1991/autor.texto: Instituto Nacional de Estadística y Censos

fuentes/censo-1991/resumen.texto: Eighth national census, taken in May 1991, at the beginning of convertibility. It recorded 32,615,528 inhabitants.

fuentes/censo-1991/por_que_importa.texto: It measures the population after hyperinflation and before the reforms of the 1990s.

fuentes/censo-2001/titulo.texto: National Census of Population, Households and Housing (2001)

fuentes/censo-2001/autor.texto: Instituto Nacional de Estadística y Censos

fuentes/censo-2001/resumen.texto: Ninth national census, taken in November 2001, a month before the outbreak of the crisis. It recorded 36,260,130 inhabitants.

fuentes/censo-2001/por_que_importa.texto: It is the statistical snapshot of the country at the end of convertibility.

fuentes/censo-2010/titulo.texto: National Census of Population, Households and Housing (2010)

fuentes/censo-2010/autor.texto: Instituto Nacional de Estadística y Censos

fuentes/censo-2010/resumen.texto: Tenth national census, taken on October 27, 2010, the same day Néstor Kirchner died. It recorded 40,117,096 inhabitants and for the first time asked about Afro-descendant ancestry.

fuentes/censo-2010/por_que_importa.texto: It measures the population during the Kirchnerist period and provides the basis for the projections of the following decade.

fuentes/censo-2022/titulo.texto: National Census of Population, Households and Housing (2022)

fuentes/censo-2022/autor.texto: Instituto Nacional de Estadística y Censos

fuentes/censo-2022/resumen.texto: Eleventh national census, taken on May 18, 2022, the first with the option of responding online and with a question on gender identity. Its final results recorded 45,892,285 enumerated inhabitants; the provisional results had given 46,044,703.

fuentes/censo-2022/por_que_importa.texto: It is the most recent measurement of the Argentine population.

personas/avellaneda/resumen.texto: President from 1874 to 1880. He enacted the Ley de Inmigración y Colonización of 1876 and in 1880 federalized the city of Buenos Aires. He was the son of Marco Avellaneda, a Unitarian of the Coalición del Norte executed in Metán in 1841.

personas/roca/resumen.texto: General who, as Avellaneda’s minister of war, led the 1879 campaign of the Conquest of the Desert, and president in 1880-1886 and 1898-1904. He was a central figure of the conservative order and of the Generation of ’80, and of the Partido Autonomista Nacional.

personas/juarez-celman/resumen.texto: President from 1886 to 1890, he and Roca were married to two Funes sisters. His government ended with the financial crisis of 1890 and the Revolution of the Park, after which he resigned.

personas/pellegrini/resumen.texto: Vice president under Juárez Celman, he completed his term after the Revolution of the Park (1890-1892) and faced the financial crisis; in 1891 he founded the Banco de la Nación Argentina.

personas/leandro-alem/resumen.texto: President of the Unión Cívica, founded in 1890 on the basis of the Unión Cívica de la Juventud (1889), and founder of the Unión Cívica Radical (1891). He led the Park Revolution of 1890 and killed himself in 1896. He was the son of Leandro Alén, a member of the Mazorca executed by firing squad in 1853; he changed the spelling of the surname.

personas/yrigoyen/resumen.texto: Leader of the Unión Cívica Radical and the first president elected under the Sáenz Peña law (1916-1922); he won again in 1928 and was overthrown by the coup of September 6, 1930. The repressions of the Tragic Week (1919) and of the Patagonia strikes (1921-1922) took place during his first government.

personas/roque-saenz-pena/resumen.texto: President from 1910 until his death in 1914. He promoted Law 8871 of 1912, which established secret and compulsory voting for male citizens and opened the way for Radicalism to reach government.

personas/alvear/resumen.texto: Radical president from 1922 to 1928, linked to the anti-personalist faction opposed to Yrigoyen; during the Infamous Decade he led the UCR.

personas/juan-b-justo/resumen.texto: Physician, founder of the Partido Socialista (1896) and of the newspaper La Vanguardia (1894). He translated the first volume of Marx's Capital directly from German (1898) and advocated a reformist, parliamentary socialism.

personas/alicia-moreau/resumen.texto: Physician and socialist leader, one of the first advocates of women's suffrage in Argentina; wife of Juan B. Justo.

personas/alfredo-palacios/resumen.texto: Socialist lawyer, elected deputy for La Boca in 1904, the first socialist deputy in the Americas. He promoted the first labor laws, such as the Sunday rest law (1905).

personas/lisandro-de-la-torre/resumen.texto: Founder of the Partido Demócrata Progresista. As a senator he denounced in 1935 the meat trade protected by the Roca–Runciman Treaty; during that debate his colleague Enzo Bordabehere was assassinated. He took his own life in 1939.

personas/ramon-falcon/resumen.texto: Chief of the Capital Police who directed the repression of the workers' rally of May 1, 1909, which left several dead; he was assassinated by Simón Radowitzky in November of that year.

personas/radowitzky/resumen.texto: Jewish anarchist born in the Russian Empire who in 1909 killed police chief Ramón Falcón with a bomb. He spent twenty-one years in prison, from 1911 in the Ushuaia penitentiary, until Yrigoyen pardoned him in 1930.

personas/deodoro-roca/resumen.texto: Lawyer from Córdoba, author of the Manifiesto Liminar of the University Reform of 1918.

personas/hector-varela/resumen.texto: Lieutenant colonel who directed the repression of the rural strikes in Santa Cruz (1921-1922), with the execution of hundreds of laborers. He was assassinated in 1923 by the anarchist Kurt Wilckens.

personas/kurt-wilckens/resumen.texto: German anarchist who in January 1923 killed Héctor Varela to avenge the executions in Patagonia; months later he was murdered in prison.

personas/osvaldo-bayer/resumen.texto: Historian and journalist, author of La Patagonia rebelde (1972-1978) and of studies on Argentine anarchism, such as Severino Di Giovanni. Threatened by the Triple A, he lived in exile in Germany during the dictatorship.

personas/lugones/resumen.texto: Modernist poet who moved from socialism to authoritarian nationalism. In his Ayacucho speech (1924) he proclaimed that “the hour of the sword” had struck, and he supported the 1930 coup.

personas/uriburu/resumen.texto: General who led the coup of September 6, 1930, against Yrigoyen and ruled de facto until 1932, with a corporatist project that did not succeed.

personas/justo/resumen.texto: General elected president in 1931, with the Yrigoyenist Radicals abstaining, and president from 1932 to 1938. His government signed the Roca–Runciman Treaty and is at the center of the so-called Infamous Decade.

personas/ramon-castillo/resumen.texto: Last president of the Infamous Decade (1940-1943), he maintained neutrality in the Second World War and was overthrown by the coup of June 4, 1943.

personas/saavedra-lamas/resumen.texto: Foreign minister under Justo (1932-1938), promoter of the Anti-War Treaty of Non-Aggression and Conciliation (1933) and mediator in the peace of the Chaco War between Bolivia and Paraguay. He was the first Latin American to receive the Nobel Peace Prize (1936).

personas/pedro-pablo-ramirez/resumen.texto: General who served as de facto president after the 1943 coup. He broke relations with the Axis in January 1944 and a month later was ousted by the GOU.

personas/farrell/resumen.texto: General who served as de facto president from 1944 to 1946, with Perón as vice president, minister of War and secretary of Labor. In March 1945 he declared war on Germany and Japan.

personas/peron/resumen.texto: Military officer and founder of Peronism, president from 1946 to 1955 and from 1973 to 1974. From the Secretaría de Trabajo (1943-1945) he allied himself with the trade unions; his doctrine, justicialism, presented itself as a third position between capitalism and communism based on social justice, economic independence and political sovereignty. His opponents accused him of authoritarianism, of persecuting the opposition and of controlling the press.

personas/eva-peron/resumen.texto: Actress and Perón's wife from 1945. She directed the Fundación Eva Perón and the Partido Peronista Femenino and promoted the women's suffrage law (1947); in 1951 she renounced the vice-presidential candidacy and died of cancer in 1952. Peronism venerates her as the “standard-bearer of the humble”; her critics pointed to the official cult of her figure and the discretionary management of the Foundation.

personas/cipriano-reyes/muerte.lugar.texto: Hospital Interzonal General De Agudos General San Martin

personas/cipriano-reyes/resumen.texto: Leader of the meatpacking workers of Berisso, one of the organizers of the mobilization of October 17, 1945, and founder of the Partido Laborista. He opposed its dissolution and was imprisoned from 1948 to 1955.

personas/sampay/resumen.texto: Jurist, the main doctrinal author of the 1949 Constitution, which incorporated social rights and the social function of property.

personas/carrillo/resumen.texto: Neurosurgeon and first national Minister of Public Health (1946-1954); he expanded the network of public hospitals and the health campaigns against malaria and other diseases.

personas/scalabrini-ortiz/resumen.texto: FORJA essayist who studied British capital in Argentina, especially the railways. He argued that economic dependence explained the country's backwardness, a thesis Peronism invoked when it nationalized the railways in 1948.

personas/jauretche/resumen.texto: Essayist and politician, founder of FORJA (1935) within Yrigoyenist radicalism and later close to Peronism. In books such as Manual de zonceras argentinas (1968) he criticized what he called the colonial mentality of the elites and the intelligentsia.

personas/hernandez-arregui/resumen.texto: Essayist of the so-called national left, which sought to unite Marxism with popular nationalism; author of La formación de la conciencia nacional (1960).

personas/john-william-cooke/resumen.texto: Peronist deputy and Perón's personal delegate during the resistance (1956-1959). He turned to Marxism and the Cuban Revolution and influenced the Peronist left; his correspondence with Perón was published in 1973.

personas/martinez-estrada/resumen.texto: Essayist, author of Radiografía de la pampa (1933). After 1955 he published ¿Qué es esto?, a critique of Peronism that also reproached the society that had made it possible.

personas/balbin/resumen.texto: Leader of the Unión Cívica Radical, an opponent imprisoned under the first Peronist government. He led the reconciliation with Perón in 1972-1974 and bade him farewell with the words “this old adversary bids farewell to a friend”.

personas/lonardi/resumen.texto: General who launched the September 1955 coup in Córdoba and served as de facto president for two months under the slogan “neither victors nor vanquished”, until he was displaced by Aramburu.

personas/aramburu/resumen.texto: General who served as de facto president of the Revolución Libertadora (1955-1958). He signed Decree 4161, which banned Peronist symbols, and ordered the 1956 executions; he was kidnapped and murdered by the Montoneros in 1970.

personas/rojas/resumen.texto: Admiral, de facto vice president of the Revolución Libertadora (1955-1958) and a leading figure of military anti-Peronism.

personas/juan-jose-valle/resumen.texto: Peronist general who led the uprising of June 9, 1956, against the Revolución Libertadora; he was executed by firing squad on June 12.

personas/frondizi/resumen.texto: President from 1958 to 1962 for the UCR Intransigente, elected with the Peronist vote that Perón ordered from exile. He applied developmentalism, with foreign investment in oil, steel and automobiles, and was overthrown by the military in 1962.

personas/rogelio-frigerio/resumen.texto: Ideologist of developmentalism and Frondizi's chief adviser; he negotiated Peronist support for Frondizi with Perón in 1958.

personas/illia/resumen.texto: Radical physician, president from 1963 to 1966, elected while Peronism was banned. He annulled Frondizi's oil contracts and was overthrown by the 1966 coup.

personas/ongania/resumen.texto: General who led the Argentine Revolution (1966-1970), a dictatorship that dissolved the political parties and took over the universities; the 1969 Cordobazo hastened his fall.

personas/lanusse/resumen.texto: Last de facto president of the Argentine Revolution (1971-1973). He negotiated the return to elections and lifted the ban on Peronism, although he blocked Perón's candidacy.

personas/tosco/resumen.texto: Leader of the Luz y Fuerza union of Córdoba, one of the leaders of the Cordobazo (1969) and a leading figure of combative trade unionism.

personas/firmenich/resumen.texto: Leader of the Montoneros; he took part in the kidnapping and murder of Aramburu (1970). He was convicted in 1987 and pardoned by Menem in 1990.

personas/santucho/resumen.texto: Founder of the Partido Revolucionario de los Trabajadores and leader of its armed wing, the ERP; he died in a clash with the Army in July 1976.

personas/campora/resumen.texto: Perón's delegate, he won the March 1973 elections under the slogan “Cámpora to government, Perón to power”; he governed for 49 days and resigned so that new elections could be called with Perón as candidate.

personas/rucci/resumen.texto: Secretary general of the CGT (1970-1973), close to Perón; he was murdered on September 25, 1973, in an attack attributed to the Montoneros.

personas/lopez-rega/resumen.texto: Perón's private secretary and Minister of Social Welfare (1973-1975). He organized the Triple A, the Argentine Anticommunist Alliance, which murdered hundreds of left-wing activists and opponents; he died in 1989 while awaiting trial.

personas/isabel-peron/resumen.texto: María Estela Martínez, Perón's third wife. Vice president in 1973 and president after her husband's death (1974-1976), the first woman in the world to hold the title of president; she was overthrown by the coup of March 24, 1976.

personas/videla/resumen.texto: General, head of the Military Junta that staged the 1976 coup and de facto president until 1981. Sentenced to life imprisonment in the Trial of the Juntas (1985), pardoned in 1990 and convicted again for crimes against humanity; he died in prison in 2013.

personas/massera/resumen.texto: Admiral of the first Military Junta (1976-1978), under whose command the ESMA clandestine detention center operated. Sentenced to life imprisonment in 1985 and pardoned in 1990.

personas/agosti/resumen.texto: Brigadier, head of the Air Force in the first Military Junta; in the Trial of the Juntas he was sentenced to four years and six months.

personas/martinez-de-hoz/resumen.texto: Minister of Economy of the dictatorship (1976-1981). He implemented trade and financial liberalization and the exchange-rate “tablita”; his critics blame him for foreign indebtedness and deindustrialization.

personas/galtieri/resumen.texto: General, de facto president (1981-1982) who ordered the occupation of the Falkland Islands in April 1982; he resigned after the defeat.

personas/bignone/resumen.texto: Last de facto president (1982-1983), he handed power to Alfonsín; from 2010 on he was convicted several times for crimes against humanity.

personas/azucena-villaflor/resumen.texto: Founder of the Mothers of the Plaza de Mayo (April 30, 1977). She was abducted in December 1977 by an ESMA group infiltrated by Alfredo Astiz; her remains were identified in 2005.

personas/hebe-de-bonafini/resumen.texto: Mother of two disappeared sons and president of the Asociación Madres de Plaza de Mayo from 1979. In her later years she supported Kirchnerism; her association was investigated over the handling of funds from the Sueños Compartidos housing program.

personas/estela-de-carlotto/resumen.texto: President of the Grandmothers of the Plaza de Mayo since 1989. Her daughter Laura was abducted while pregnant and murdered in 1978; her grandson, Ignacio Montoya Carlotto, recovered his identity in 2014.

personas/rodolfo-walsh/resumen.texto: Journalist and writer, a pioneer of investigative journalism with Operation Massacre (1957). He was a member of the Montoneros and was ambushed and killed by an ESMA task force on March 25, 1977, one day after sending his Open Letter to the Military Junta.

personas/perez-esquivel/resumen.texto: Architect and sculptor, coordinator of the Servicio Paz y Justicia. He was imprisoned without trial during the dictatorship (1977-1978) and received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1980 for his nonviolent defense of human rights.

personas/strassera/resumen.texto: Prosecutor in the Trial of the Juntas (1985); he closed his summation with the words “Your Honors: never again”.

personas/moreno-ocampo/resumen.texto: Deputy prosecutor in the Trial of the Juntas and, from 2003 to 2012, first prosecutor of the International Criminal Court.

personas/alfonsin/resumen.texto: Radical leader, first president of the restored democracy (1983-1989). He created CONADEP and promoted the Trial of the Juntas, but later pushed the Full Stop and Due Obedience laws; he handed over the government early amid hyperinflation.

personas/menem/resumen.texto: Peronist leader from La Rioja, president from 1989 to 1999. He privatized state companies, established convertibility and pardoned military leaders and guerrillas; his supporters highlight price stability, and his critics, unemployment, indebtedness and corruption.

personas/cavallo/resumen.texto: Minister of Economy under Menem (1991-1996), author of convertibility, and under De la Rúa in 2001, when he imposed the banking “corralito”.

personas/de-la-rua/resumen.texto: Radical leader, president for the Alianza (1999-2001). He resigned on December 20, 2001, amid a social uprising and a crackdown that left dozens dead.

personas/rodriguez-saa/resumen.texto: Governor of San Luis, president for one week in December 2001; he announced the suspension of public debt payments.
