personas/duhalde/resumen.texto: Peronist leader from Buenos Aires Province elected president by Congress in January 2002. He ended convertibility, converted the economy to pesos and brought forward the elections after the Avellaneda massacre.

personas/nestor-kirchner/resumen.texto: Governor of Santa Cruz and president from 2003 to 2007. He restructured the defaulted debt, paid off the debt to the IMF and promoted the reopening of trials for the dictatorship's crimes. He gave his name to Kirchnerism, which his supporters see as a national and popular project and his critics associate with corruption in public works and the manipulation of official statistics.

personas/cristina-kirchner/resumen.texto: President from 2007 to 2015 and vice president from 2019 to 2023; she has chaired the Partido Justicialista since December 2024. She was sentenced to six years in prison and a lifetime ban from public office in the Vialidad case, final since June 2025, and is serving the sentence at home; she maintains that she is a victim of “lawfare”, a judicial and media persecution.

personas/boudou/resumen.texto: Head of ANSES during the nationalization of the AFJP pension funds (2008), Minister of Economy (2009-2011) and vice president (2011-2015). Sentenced in the Ciccone case to five years and ten months in prison, the first vice president with a final conviction.

personas/de-vido/resumen.texto: Minister of Federal Planning under Néstor and Cristina Kirchner (2003-2015), in charge of public works, energy and transport. Convicted over the Once tragedy, with a final sentence in 2025, and in other cases; he maintains his innocence.

personas/ricardo-jaime/resumen.texto: Secretary of Transport (2003-2009). He was convicted over the Once tragedy (2015) and in other cases for accepting gifts and illicit enrichment.

personas/lazaro-baez/resumen.texto: Businessman from Santa Cruz, owner of Austral Construcciones, which received a large share of Santa Cruz's road works during the Kirchner governments. Convicted of money laundering (the “K money trail”) and in the Vialidad case.

personas/jose-lopez/resumen.texto: Secretary of Public Works (2003-2015). In June 2016 he was arrested while trying to hide bags containing nearly nine million dollars in a convent in General Rodríguez; convicted of illicit enrichment and in the Vialidad case.

personas/timerman/resumen.texto: Foreign minister under Cristina Kirchner (2010-2015) who signed the Memorandum of Understanding with Iran in 2013; he was indicted for cover-up and died in 2018 before going to trial.

personas/nisman/resumen.texto: Prosecutor in charge of the AMIA case from 2004. In January 2015 he accused Cristina Kirchner of a cover-up through the Memorandum with Iran, and four days later he was found dead of a gunshot wound in his apartment.

personas/bonadio/resumen.texto: Federal judge (1994-2020) who investigated the Notebooks, Los Sauces and Memorandum cases against Cristina Kirchner, who sought his recusal and accused him of bias.

personas/milagro-sala/resumen.texto: Founder of the Tupac Amaru organization in Jujuy. Detained since 2016, she was convicted of fraud with housing funds, extortion and criminal association and given a combined sentence of fifteen years, final since 2025; she and human rights organizations consider her a political prisoner, and a UN working group described her detention as arbitrary.

personas/macri/resumen.texto: Businessman, head of government of Buenos Aires City (2007-2015), founder of PRO and president from 2015 to 2019 for Cambiemos. He lifted currency controls, paid the holdout creditors and in 2018 signed a $57 billion loan with the IMF; his supporters highlight the opening of the economy, and his critics, the rise in debt and poverty.

personas/alberto-fernandez/resumen.texto: Cabinet chief under Néstor Kirchner and president from 2019 to 2023, with Cristina Kirchner as vice president; he governed during the COVID-19 pandemic and rising inflation. He was later indicted for gender-based violence against his former wife and investigated over the contracting of state insurance; he denies the charges.

personas/massa/resumen.texto: Minister of Economy (2022-2023) and presidential candidate of Unión por la Patria, defeated by Milei in the 2023 runoff.

personas/kicillof/resumen.texto: Minister of Economy under Cristina Kirchner (2013-2015), promoter of the expropriation of YPF, and governor of Buenos Aires Province since 2019.

personas/milei/resumen.texto: Economist who describes himself as an anarcho-capitalist, deputy (2021-2023) and president since December 10, 2023, for La Libertad Avanza. He is carrying out broad fiscal austerity and deregulation; his supporters highlight the fall in inflation and the fiscal surplus, and his critics, the decline in consumption and employment and the cuts to universities, health care and disability programs.

personas/villarruel/resumen.texto: Vice president since 2023. She previously chaired the Centro de Estudios Legales sobre el Terrorismo y sus Víctimas, which advocates for the victims of the 1970s guerrillas; she soon distanced herself from Milei.

personas/bullrich/resumen.texto: Minister of Security under Macri (2015-2019) and Milei (2023-2025), presidential candidate of Juntos por el Cambio in 2023 and senator for the City of Buenos Aires since December 2025.

personas/caputo/resumen.texto: Minister of Finance under Macri and president of the Central Bank in 2018; Minister of Economy under Milei since 2023.

personas/houssay/resumen.texto: Physiologist, Nobel Prize in Medicine in 1947 for the role of the pituitary gland in sugar metabolism. He was removed from his chair in 1943 and again in 1946; in 1958 he founded CONICET and presided over it until his death.

personas/leloir/resumen.texto: Biochemist born in Paris, a disciple of Houssay, Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1970 for the discovery of sugar nucleotides and their role in the biosynthesis of carbohydrates; he directed the Instituto de Investigaciones Bioquímicas Fundación Campomar.

personas/milstein/resumen.texto: Biochemist from Bahía Blanca who left the Instituto Malbrán in 1963 and worked in Cambridge. With Georges Köhler he developed the monoclonal antibody technique in 1975, for which they shared the 1984 Nobel Prize in Medicine.

personas/favaloro/resumen.texto: Surgeon from La Plata who in 1967, at the Cleveland Clinic, standardized coronary artery bypass surgery using the saphenous vein. Back in Argentina he created the Fundación Favaloro; he took his own life in 2000, amid his institution's financial crisis.

personas/sadosky/resumen.texto: Mathematician and promoter of computing in Argentina: he directed the Instituto de Cálculo of the UBA, where the Clementina computer operated from 1961. He resigned after the Night of the Long Batons (1966) and under Alfonsín served as Secretary of Science and Technology.

personas/biro/resumen.texto: Hungarian journalist and inventor who settled in Argentina in 1940, where in 1943 he patented the viscous-ink ballpoint pen known as the birome.

personas/richter/resumen.texto: Austrian physicist who persuaded Perón to fund a controlled nuclear fusion project on Huemul Island; the 1951 announcement proved unfounded and the project was shut down in 1952.

personas/balseiro/resumen.texto: Physicist who served on the commission that evaluated the Huemul Project and in 1955 founded the Instituto de Física de Bariloche, which now bears his name.

hechos/conquista-del-desierto/resumen.texto: Military campaigns of the Argentine state over the Pampas and Patagonia between 1878 and 1885; the one of 1879, led by Roca as Minister of War, reached the Río Negro. In Chubut, during the last campaigns, a group of Indigenous people killed three Welsh colonists in the Valle de los Mártires in 1884. For 1878 and 1879 the Memoria del Departamento de Guerra counted 1,313 Indigenous people “de lanza” killed, 1,271 lanza prisoners and 10,513 “de chusma” (women, children and elderly) taken prisoner, not counting the later deaths of the prisoners, who were confined or distributed as labor; the lands passed to the State and then, in large part, to private hands. The governments of the time and military historiography present it as the incorporation of the territory; the Indigenous peoples and part of academic historiography call it genocide, a term other historians reject.

hechos/federalizacion-de-buenos-aires/lu.texto: Belgrano Town Hall (now the Sarmiento Historical Museum), Buenos Aires

hechos/federalizacion-de-buenos-aires/re.texto: After the defeat of Buenos Aires Province in the revolution of 1880, Congress declared the city the capital of the Republic; the province founded La Plata as its new capital in 1882.

hechos/inmigracion-masiva/resumen.texto: Between 1880 and 1930 about six million immigrants arrived in the country, of whom more than half stayed, mostly Italians and Spaniards. In 1914 foreigners made up 30 % of the population and nearly half of the inhabitants of Buenos Aires. Before the great wave, mainly between 1850 and 1870, thousands of Irish had arrived in the Buenos Aires countryside, and in 1865 the first Welsh colonists arrived in Chubut.

hechos/ley-1420-sancion/titulo.texto: Passage of Law 1420 on common education

hechos/ley-1420-sancion/lugar.texto: Old National Congress building, Buenos Aires

hechos/ley-1420-sancion/resumen.texto: In 1884, after a long debate with the Catholic deputies, Congress approved common, free and compulsory primary education, with religious instruction outside class hours (which is why it is called secular, although the law does not use that word); the conflict with the Church, aggravated by the case of the normal school of Córdoba, led to the breaking of relations with the Holy See.

hechos/revolucion-del-parque/resumen.texto: Uprising of the Unión Cívica against Juárez Celman that began on July 26, 1890, at the Artillery Park in Buenos Aires. It was defeated, but the president resigned days later amid the financial crisis, and the Unión Cívica Radical emerged from the movement.

hechos/fundacion-de-la-ucr/titulo.texto: Founding of the Unión Cívica Radical

hechos/fundacion-de-la-ucr/resumen.texto: Leandro Alem founded the UCR in 1891 when he split from the cívicos who had made a pact with Roca. Under Yrigoyen it practiced electoral abstention and armed uprisings (1893, 1905) to demand free elections.

hechos/fundacion-del-partido-socialista/.texto: Teatro Verdi, La Boca, Buenos Aires
Juan B. Justo and other activists founded the Socialist Party in 1896, with a reformist and parliamentary orientation; in 1904 it won its first deputy seat with Alfredo Palacios.

hechos/fundacion-de-la-fora/resumen.texto: The Federación Obrera Argentina, founded in 1901 and called FORA from 1904, adopted anarcho-communism as its principle in 1905. It led general strikes and was repressed with the Residence Law (1902) and the Social Defense Law (1910).

hechos/informe-bialet-masse-hecho/titulo.texto: Bialet Massé's journey through the provinces

hechos/informe-bialet-masse-hecho/resume.texto: Commissioned by Roca's government, the physician Juan Bialet Massé traveled the country to describe the conditions of workers; his report denounced exhausting working days and payment in vouchers at the sugar mills and logging camps of the north.

hechos/semana-roja/titulo.texto: Red Week and assassination of Ramón Falcón

hechos/semana-roja/resumen.texto: On May 1, 1909, Ramón Falcón's police repressed an anarchist rally in Plaza Lorea, leaving several dead, and a week-long general strike followed. On November 14 Simón Radowitzky killed Falcón with a bomb.

hechos/centenario-de-1910/resumen.texto: Celebration in May 1910, with international exhibitions and visits by heads of state, in which the elite displayed the country's growth. It took place under a state of siege: nationalist groups attacked anarchist and socialist premises, and in June, after a bomb at the Teatro Colón, the Social Defense Law was passed.

hechos/grito-de-alcorta/resumen.texto: Rebellion of tenant farmers, mostly Italian immigrants, that began in June 1912 in Alcorta (Santa Fe) against the price of land rents; it gave rise to the Federación Agraria Argentina.

hechos/ley-saenz-pena-sancion/titulo.texto: Passage of the Sáenz Peña Law

hechos/ley-saenz-pena-sancion/lugar.texto: Palace of the Argentine National Congress

hechos/ley-saenz-pena-sancion/resumen.texto: In February 1912 Congress approved secret and compulsory voting for men; that same year the elections in Santa Fe and the Capital showed the advance of radicalism and socialism.

hechos/eleccion-de-yrigoyen/resumen.texto: First presidential election under the Sáenz Peña Law; it was won by the Radical Yrigoyen, who took office on October 12, 1916, and ended the dominance of the conservative order.

hechos/reforma-universitaria/resumen.texto: Movement of the students of Córdoba that, from March 1918, demanded university autonomy, co-governance, academic freedom and competitive selection of faculty; Yrigoyen took over the university and accepted many of their demands, which spread across Latin America.

hechos/semana-tragica/resumen.texto: In January 1919 a strike at the Vasena workshops turned into a general strike repressed by the Army, the police and armed civilian groups, who also attacked the Jewish neighborhood; the dead number in the hundreds according to various estimates. Yrigoyen was in government and put General Luis Dellepiane in command of the troops in the city.

hechos/patagonia-rebelde/resumen.texto: Strikes by ranch hands on the estancias of Santa Cruz for better working conditions, repressed in 1921-1922 by the Army under Héctor Varela, sent by Yrigoyen's government; hundreds of strikers were shot, and estimates range from several hundred to more than a thousand.

hechos/masacre-de-napalpi/resumen.texto: On July 19, 1924, police and civilians at the Napalpí reservation, in the Chaco, attacked Qom and Moqoit indigenous people who were protesting their working conditions, killing several hundred. In 2022 a truth trial declared it a crime against humanity.

hechos/golpe-de-1930/resumen.texto: On September 6, 1930, General Uriburu overthrew Yrigoyen in the century's first successful military coup; the Supreme Court recognized it with a ruling (acordada) that inaugurated the doctrine of de facto governments.

hechos/decada-infame/resumen.texto: Period of conservative governments sustained by so-called “patriotic fraud”, with the Radicals banned or abstaining, which signed the Roca–Runciman Treaty. The name was popularized by the nationalist journalist José Luis Torres.

hechos/fundacion-de-forja/resumen.texto: The Fuerza de Orientación Radical de la Joven Argentina, founded in June 1935 by Jauretche, Homero Manzi, Luis Dellepiane and other Yrigoyenist Radicals, denounced dependence on British capital under the slogan “We are a colonial Argentina; we want to be a free Argentina”. It dissolved in 1945 and many of its members joined Peronism.

hechos/asesinato-de-bordabehere/titulo.texto: Assassination of Enzo Bordabehere in the Senate

hechos/asesinato-de-bordabehere/lugar.texto: Palace of the Argentine National Congress

hechos/asesinato-de-bordabehere/resumen.texto: On July 23, 1935, during the meat debate, former police superintendent Ramón Valdez Cora fired at Lisandro de la Torre on the Senate floor and killed senator-elect Enzo Bordabehere, who stepped in between.

hechos/nobel-de-saavedra-lamas/titulo.texto: Nobel Peace Prize for Carlos Saavedra Lamas

hechos/nobel-de-saavedra-lamas/resumen.texto: Saavedra Lamas received the 1936 Nobel Peace Prize for the Anti-War Treaty and his mediation in ending the Chaco War between Bolivia and Paraguay; he was the first Latin American laureate.

hechos/golpe-de-1943/resumen.texto: On June 4, 1943, a military coup, with the Grupo de Oficiales Unidos (GOU) at its core, overthrew Castillo and ended the Infamous Decade; Perón rose to prominence from within that government.

hechos/secretaria-de-trabajo/titulo.texto: Perón at the Secretaría de Trabajo y Previsión

hechos/secretaria-de-trabajo/resumen.texto: From the Departamento Nacional del Trabajo, turned into a secretariat in November 1943, Perón promoted collective bargaining agreements, the Estatuto del Peón, labor courts and the extension of pensions, and built an alliance with the trade unions.

hechos/birome/resumen.texto: In June 1943 László Bíró patented in Argentina the viscous-ink ballpoint pen that he manufactured in Buenos Aires under the name birome.

hechos/declaracion-de-guerra-de-1945/tit.texto: Argentina declares war on Germany and Japan

hechos/declaracion-de-guerra-de-1945/res.texto: On March 27, 1945, weeks before the end of the war in Europe, Farrell's government abandoned neutrality and declared war on Japan and Germany, which allowed the country to join the founding conference of the United Nations.

hechos/17-de-octubre/resumen.texto: After Perón's detention on Martín García Island, columns of workers from Greater Buenos Aires marched to the Plaza de Mayo and won his release; that night Perón spoke from the balcony of the Casa Rosada. It is the founding act of Peronism.

hechos/eleccion-de-peron/resumen.texto: On February 24, 1946, Perón, backed by the Partido Laborista and the UCR Junta Renovadora, defeated the Unión Democrática; the campaign was marked by the intervention of former US ambassador Spruille Braden and the slogan “Braden or Perón”.

hechos/nobel-de-houssay/titulo.texto: Nobel Prize in Medicine for Bernardo Houssay

hechos/nobel-de-houssay/resumen.texto: Houssay received the 1947 Nobel Prize in Medicine for his studies on the role of the pituitary gland in sugar metabolism; he was the first Latin American scientist to win a prize in the sciences.

hechos/independencia-economica/resumen.texto: On July 9, 1947, at the Casa Histórica in Tucumán, Perón signed the Declaration of Economic Independence, in the year of the purchase of the British railways and the cancellation of the foreign debt.

hechos/voto-femenino/lugar.texto: Palace of the Argentine National Congress

hechos/voto-femenino/resumen.texto: In September 1947 Congress passed Law 13,010, which gave women the right to vote and to stand for office, following a campaign by Eva Perón.

hechos/nacionalizacion-de-los-ferrocarri.texto: On March 1, 1948, the State took possession of the British-owned railways, bought with pounds accumulated from exports during the war. For Peronism it was a recovery of sovereignty; its critics pointed to the high price paid for aging equipment.

hechos/reforma-constitucional-de-1949/lu.texto: Palace of the Argentine National Congress

hechos/reforma-constitucional-de-1949/re.texto: The constitutional convention, with a Peronist majority, enacted on March 11, 1949, a constitution with social rights and indefinite reelection; the Radical delegates withdrew, questioning its legitimacy.

hechos/congreso-de-filosofia-de-1949/res.texto: Congress held in Mendoza in April 1949 with Argentine, Latin American and European philosophers; Perón closed it with the speech La comunidad organizada.

hechos/proyecto-huemul/resumen.texto: On March 24, 1951, Perón announced that Ronald Richter had achieved controlled nuclear fusion reactions on Huemul Island. A commission of scientists, including José Antonio Balseiro, determined in 1952 that this was not the case and the project was shut down; the Comisión Nacional de Energía Atómica, created in 1950, survived and established the Instituto Balseiro.

hechos/renunciamiento/resumen.texto: At the Cabildo Abierto del Justicialismo on August 22, 1951, the CGT proclaimed the Perón–Eva Perón ticket; on August 31, by radio, Eva Perón declined the vice-presidential candidacy, amid military opposition and her illness.

hechos/elecciones-de-1951/resumen.texto: On November 11, 1951, Perón was reelected with more than 60% of the vote, in the first national elections in which women voted; Eva Perón voted from her hospital bed.

hechos/muerte-de-eva-peron/resumen.texto: Eva Perón died on July 26, 1952, at the age of 33; her wake lasted almost two weeks. Her embalmed body was seized by the military in 1955, secretly buried in Milan and returned to Perón in 1971.

hechos/bombardeo-de-plaza-de-mayo/titulo.texto: Bombing of the Plaza de Mayo

hechos/bombardeo-de-plaza-de-mayo/resume.texto: On June 16, 1955, Navy and Air Force aircraft bombed and strafed the Casa Rosada and the Plaza de Mayo in order to kill Perón; more than 300 people died, most of them civilians. That night Peronist groups set fire to churches in downtown Buenos Aires.

hechos/golpe-de-1955/resumen.texto: On September 16, 1955, a military uprising launched in Córdoba by Lonardi, with the support of Rojas's Navy, overthrew Perón, who went into exile. Its supporters called it the Revolución Libertadora; Peronists called it the “Revolución Fusiladora”, and the movement remained banned until 1973.

hechos/levantamiento-de-valle/resumen.texto: On June 9, 1956, Peronist soldiers and civilians led by Juan José Valle rose up against Aramburu. The government imposed martial law and executed soldiers and civilians, among them Valle, and in a garbage dump in José León Suárez the police executed detained civilians.

hechos/resistencia-peronista/resumen.texto: Set of strikes, acts of sabotage, clandestine union organizing and armed actions with which Peronism confronted its proscription, directed from exile by Perón and, in its early years, by John William Cooke.

hechos/eleccion-de-frondizi/resumen.texto: On February 23, 1958, Frondizi won the presidency with the Peronist vote that Perón ordered from exile, following a pact negotiated by Rogelio Frigerio.

hechos/fundacion-del-conicet/resumen.texto: The Consejo Nacional de Investigaciones Científicas y Técnicas was created in February 1958 and presided over by Bernardo Houssay until his death; it established the career track for research scientists.

hechos/clementina/titulo.texto: Clementina, the country's first scientific computer

hechos/clementina/resumen.texto: A Ferranti Mercury computer, named Clementina, began operating in 1961 at the Instituto de Cálculo of the Facultad de Ciencias Exactas of the UBA, directed by Manuel Sadosky; it was the basis for the country's first computer science degree.

hechos/golpe-de-1962/resumen.texto: After the Peronist victory in the March 1962 elections, including that of Andrés Framini in Buenos Aires Province, the military removed Frondizi on March 29 and detained him on Martín García Island; the president of the Senate, José María Guido, took office.

hechos/golpe-de-1966/resumen.texto: On June 28, 1966, the military commanders overthrew Illia and installed Onganía with a plan for an open-ended dictatorship that dissolved the political parties.

hechos/noche-de-los-bastones-largos/resu.texto: On July 29, 1966, police violently evicted five UBA faculties occupied in protest against the government takeover of the universities. Hundreds of professors resigned and many scientists emigrated.

hechos/bypass-de-favaloro/resumen.texto: In May 1967, at the Cleveland Clinic, René Favaloro operated on a patient using a saphenous vein graft to get around a coronary obstruction; the technique spread worldwide as the bypass.

hechos/cordobazo/resumen.texto: On May 29 and 30, 1969, workers from the automotive plants and Luz y Fuerza, together with students, staged a strike and popular uprising in Córdoba that the Army repressed; it weakened Onganía, who fell the following year.

hechos/asesinato-de-aramburu/resumen.texto: On May 29, 1970, a Montoneros commando kidnapped Pedro Eugenio Aramburu from his home; they killed him on June 1 at a ranch in Timote. It was the organization's public debut.

hechos/nobel-de-leloir/titulo.texto: Nobel Prize in Chemistry for Luis Federico Leloir

hechos/nobel-de-leloir/resumen.texto: Leloir received the 1970 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for the discovery of sugar nucleotides and their role in the biosynthesis of carbohydrates, researched in a modest laboratory in Buenos Aires.

hechos/masacre-de-trelew/resumen.texto: On August 22, 1972, navy men at the Almirante Zar base shot 19 prisoners from Montoneros, FAR and ERP who had been recaptured after an escape from the Rawson prison; 16 died. In 2012 a court sentenced three navy men to life imprisonment.

hechos/regreso-de-peron/resumen.texto: On November 17, 1972, after seventeen years of exile, Perón returned to the country for a few weeks; he met with Balbín and formed the Frente Justicialista de Liberación.

hechos/eleccion-de-campora/resumen.texto: On March 11, 1973, the Frente Justicialista de Liberación, with Cámpora as its candidate, won with almost half the vote; Cámpora took office on May 25 and granted amnesty to political prisoners.

hechos/masacre-de-ezeiza/resumen.texto: On June 20, 1973, during Perón's definitive return, groups from the union sector and the Peronist right fired from the stage at columns of the Peronist Youth and Montoneros; at least 13 people died and hundreds were wounded.

hechos/asesinato-de-rucci/resumen.texto: On September 25, 1973, two days after Perón's election, a commando killed the secretary general of the CGT, José Ignacio Rucci; the crime is attributed to Montoneros, which never publicly claimed responsibility.

hechos/tercera-presidencia-de-peron/titu.texto: Election of Perón to his third presidency

hechos/tercera-presidencia-de-peron/resu.texto: On September 23, 1973, the Perón–Isabel Perón ticket won with 62% of the vote; Perón took office on October 12.

hechos/ruptura-con-montoneros/resumen.texto: At the Labor Day rally Perón called the Montoneros militants “beardless youths”, and they walked out of the Plaza de Mayo; months later the organization returned to clandestinity.

hechos/atucha-i/resumen.texto: The Atucha I nuclear power plant, in Lima, Zárate district, began operating in 1974; it was the first nuclear power plant in Latin America.

hechos/muerte-de-peron/resumen.texto: Perón died at the Quinta de Olivos on July 1, 1974; his widow, Vice President Isabel Perón, assumed the presidency, and Balbín bade him farewell in Congress as “a friend”.

hechos/triple-a/resumen.texto: The Argentine Anticommunist Alliance, organized from López Rega's Ministry of Social Welfare, murdered hundreds of left-wing militants, trade unionists, intellectuals and opponents between 1973 and 1976.

hechos/operativo-independencia/resumen.texto: Under a February 1975 decree of Isabel Perón's government, the Army operated in Tucumán to “neutralize and/or annihilate” the ERP guerrillas; the first clandestine detention centers operated there.

hechos/rodrigazo/resumen.texto: In June 1975 Minister Celestino Rodrigo imposed a sharp devaluation and increases in utility rates and fuel prices; the CGT responded with the first general strike against a Peronist government, and Rodrigo and López Rega left the government.

hechos/golpe-de-1976/resumen.texto: On March 24, 1976, the Junta of Videla, Massera and Agosti overthrew Isabel Perón and began the National Reorganization Process, which ruled until 1983.

hechos/terrorismo-de-estado/resumen.texto: The dictatorship kidnapped, tortured and murdered militants, trade unionists, students and others in hundreds of clandestine centers and appropriated some five hundred children of detained women. CONADEP documented 8,961 disappeared; human rights organizations maintain the figure of 30,000, which other sectors dispute.

hechos/noche-de-los-lapices/resumen.texto: In September 1976 the Buenos Aires Province police kidnapped in La Plata secondary school students who had demanded a student transit fare; six remain disappeared.

hechos/madres-de-plaza-de-mayo/titulo.texto: First march of the Mothers of the Plaza de Mayo

hechos/madres-de-plaza-de-mayo/resumen.texto: On April 30, 1977, fourteen mothers of disappeared people, called together by Azucena Villaflor, gathered in the Plaza de Mayo to demand answers about their children; since then they have marched every Thursday wearing white headscarves.

hechos/abuelas-de-plaza-de-mayo/titulo.texto: Founding of the Grandmothers of the Plaza de Mayo

hechos/abuelas-de-plaza-de-mayo/resumen.texto: In October 1977 a group of grandmothers began searching for the grandchildren born in captivity or abducted with their parents; with the help of genetic databanks they have restored the identity of more than 130 of them.

hechos/asesinato-de-walsh/resumen.texto: On March 25, 1977, one day after sending his Open Letter to the Military Junta, Walsh was ambushed by an ESMA task force and killed; his remains were never found.

hechos/mundial-78/resumen.texto: Argentina hosted and won the championship while the clandestine centers were operating; the dictatorship used it as propaganda against what it called the “anti-Argentine campaign” abroad.

hechos/conflicto-del-beagle/resumen.texto: In December 1978 Argentina and Chile came to the brink of war over the islands of the Beagle Channel; the mediation of Pope John Paul II averted it and led to the 1984 Treaty of Peace and Friendship, approved in Argentina by popular referendum.

hechos/visita-de-la-cidh/titulo.texto: Visit of the Inter-American Commission on Human Rights

hechos/visita-de-la-cidh/resumen.texto: In September 1979 the IACHR received thousands of complaints in Buenos Aires and other cities; its 1980 report confirmed the systematic practice of enforced disappearance.

hechos/nobel-de-perez-esquivel/titulo.texto: Nobel Peace Prize for Adolfo Pérez Esquivel

hechos/nobel-de-perez-esquivel/resumen.texto: The Norwegian committee awarded the prize in 1980 to Pérez Esquivel for his nonviolent defense of human rights in Latin America, in the midst of the dictatorship.

hechos/guerra-de-malvinas/resumen.texto: On April 2, 1982, Argentine troops occupied the Falkland Islands (Malvinas) on Galtieri's orders; the United Kingdom sent a task force and retook the islands with the surrender of Puerto Argentino (Stanley) on June 14. The war killed 649 Argentines, 255 Britons and 3 islanders, and the defeat hastened the end of the dictatorship.

hechos/hundimiento-del-belgrano/titulo.texto: Sinking of the cruiser General Belgrano

hechos/hundimiento-del-belgrano/resumen.texto: On May 2, 1982, the British submarine Conqueror torpedoed the cruiser General Belgrano outside the exclusion zone declared by the United Kingdom; 323 crew members died, almost half of Argentina's casualties in the war.

hechos/recuperacion-de-la-democracia/tit.texto: 1983 elections and the return of democracy

hechos/recuperacion-de-la-democracia/res.texto: On October 30, 1983, Raúl Alfonsín won the presidency with more than 50% of the vote, Peronism's first defeat in free elections; he took office on December 10.

hechos/conadep/titulo.texto: Comisión Nacional sobre la Desaparición de Personas

hechos/conadep/resumen.texto: Commission created by Alfonsín in December 1983 and chaired by Ernesto Sabato that gathered testimonies, inspected clandestine centers and in September 1984 delivered the Nunca más report.

hechos/nobel-de-milstein/titulo.texto: Nobel Prize in Medicine for César Milstein

hechos/nobel-de-milstein/resumen.texto: Milstein shared the 1984 Nobel Prize in Medicine with Georges Köhler and Niels Jerne for the monoclonal antibody technique.

hechos/juicio-a-las-juntas/lugar.texto: Palacio de Justicia de la Nación (Tribunales)

hechos/juicio-a-las-juntas/resumen.texto: Between April 22 and December 9, 1985, the Federal Court of Appeals of Buenos Aires tried the nine members of the first three juntas for 709 cases; prosecutor Strassera closed his argument with “Never again”. Five were convicted and four acquitted.

hechos/plan-austral-hecho/resumen.texto: On June 14, 1985, Alfonsín's government changed the currency and froze prices and wages; inflation fell drastically for a year and rose again from 1987.

hechos/levantamiento-de-semana-santa/res.texto: In April 1987 officers led by Aldo Rico rebelled at Campo de Mayo against the trials; society mobilized in defense of democracy and Alfonsín announced “the house is in order”, but weeks later the Obediencia Debida law was passed.

hechos/hiperinflacion-de-1989/resumen.texto: Annual inflation exceeded 3,000% in 1989, with looting of shops and a state of siege; Alfonsín handed power to Menem on July 8, five months ahead of schedule.

hechos/indultos/resumen.texto: Between October 1989 and December 1990 Menem pardoned the military chiefs convicted in the Trial of the Juntas, the carapintadas, the commanders of the Falklands/Malvinas War and guerrilla leaders; there were large marches against them.

hechos/convertibilidad/resumen.texto: On April 1, 1991, the fixed parity with the dollar came into force, ending hyperinflation; in the second half of the decade unemployment and debt grew, and the regime collapsed with the 2001 crisis.

hechos/privatizaciones/resumen.texto: Under the Ley de Reforma del Estado of 1989, Menem's government sold or granted concessions for ENTel, Aerolíneas Argentinas, the railways, gas, electricity, water and YPF, which passed to the Spanish company Repsol in 1999, and in 1994 it created private pension funds (AFJP).

hechos/pacto-de-olivos-hecho/resumen.texto: On November 14, 1993, Menem and Alfonsín agreed at the Quinta de Olivos to amend the Constitution to allow presidential reelection in exchange for institutional reforms.

hechos/reforma-constitucional-de-1994/re.texto: The convention meeting in Santa Fe and Paraná enacted on August 22, 1994, the reform agreed at Olivos; Menem was reelected in 1995.

hechos/crisis-de-2001/resumen.texto: Following the corralito, on December 19 and 20, 2001, there were lootings, pot-banging protests with the cry “they all must go” and a crackdown that left 39 dead nationwide; De la Rúa resigned and five presidents succeeded one another in twelve days.

hechos/default-de-2001/lugar.texto: Palace of the Argentine National Congress

hechos/default-de-2001/resumen.texto: On December 23, 2001, President Adolfo Rodríguez Saá announced before the Legislative Assembly the suspension of payments on the public debt, some 100 billion dollars, the largest sovereign default up to that time.

hechos/fin-de-la-convertibilidad/lugar.texto: Palace of the Argentine National Congress

hechos/fin-de-la-convertibilidad/resumen.texto: In January 2002 the Ley de Emergencia Pública of Duhalde's government ended the fixed parity; devaluation and the pesification of deposits and debts followed, and poverty exceeded half the population that year.

hechos/masacre-de-avellaneda/resumen.texto: On June 26, 2002, the Buenos Aires Province police killed the piquetero activists Maximiliano Kosteki and Darío Santillán during a blockade of the Pueyrredón bridge; police superintendent Alfredo Fanchiotti was sentenced to life imprisonment, and Duhalde brought the elections forward.

hechos/eleccion-de-nestor-kirchner/titul.texto: Néstor Kirchner comes to the presidency

hechos/eleccion-de-nestor-kirchner/lugar.texto: Palace of the Argentine National Congress

hechos/eleccion-de-nestor-kirchner/resum.texto: In the election of April 27, 2003, Menem came first and Kirchner second, with 22% of the vote; Menem withdrew from the runoff and Kirchner took office on May 25.

hechos/nulidad-de-las-leyes-de-impunidad.texto: Annulment of the Punto Final and Obediencia Debida laws
Palace of the Argentine National Congress
In August 2003, at Kirchner's request, Congress annulled the Punto Final and Obediencia Debida laws, which made it possible to reopen proceedings for the crimes of the dictatorship.

hechos/fallo-simon-hecho/titulo.texto: Simón ruling: reopening of the crimes against humanity trials

hechos/fallo-simon-hecho/lugar.texto: Palacio de Justicia de la Nación (Tribunales)

hechos/fallo-simon-hecho/resumen.texto: On June 14, 2005, the Supreme Court declared the impunity laws unconstitutional; since 2006 federal courts have tried more than a thousand defendants for crimes against humanity.

hechos/pago-al-fmi/resumen.texto: On January 3, 2006, Néstor Kirchner's government paid off in advance, with Central Bank reserves, its entire debt to the International Monetary Fund, about 10 billion dollars.

hechos/juicio-a-etchecolatz/titulo.texto: Conviction of Etchecolatz and disappearance of Jorge Julio López

hechos/juicio-a-etchecolatz/resumen.texto: On September 19, 2006, former police superintendent Miguel Etchecolatz was sentenced to life imprisonment in the first trial after the reopening, for crimes committed “in the framework of a genocide”; the day before, Jorge Julio López, a key witness in the trial, had disappeared, and he was never found.

hechos/conflicto-del-campo/lugar.texto: Palace of the Argentine National Congress

hechos/conflicto-del-campo/resumen.texto: For 129 days the farm organizations opposed the sliding export duties, with road blockades and mass rallies; on July 17, 2008, Vice President Cobos cast the tie-breaking vote against them in the Senate.

hechos/estatizacion-de-las-afjp/lugar.texto: Palace of the Argentine National Congress

hechos/estatizacion-de-las-afjp/resumen.texto: In November 2008 the government of Cristina Kirchner abolished private pensions and transferred their funds to ANSES.

hechos/ley-de-medios-hecho/titulo.texto: Media Law and the conflict with Grupo Clarín

hechos/ley-de-medios-hecho/lugar.texto: Palace of the Argentine National Congress

hechos/ley-de-medios-hecho/resumen.texto: In October 2009 Congress passed the Ley de Servicios de Comunicación Audiovisual amid the confrontation between the government of Cristina Kirchner and Grupo Clarín.

hechos/matrimonio-igualitario/lugar.texto: Palace of the Argentine National Congress

hechos/matrimonio-igualitario/resumen.texto: On 15 July 2010 the Senate approved same-sex marriage, the first nationwide in Latin America.

hechos/muerte-de-nestor-kirchner/resumen.texto: Néstor Kirchner died of cardiac arrest on 27 October 2010 in El Calafate, on the day of the national census; his wake at the Casa Rosada drew huge crowds.

hechos/tragedia-de-once/resumen.texto: On 22 February 2012 a Sarmiento line train failed to brake and crashed into the end of the platform at Once station; 52 people died and more than 700 were injured.

hechos/expropiacion-de-ypf/lugar.texto: Palace of the Argentine National Congress

hechos/expropiacion-de-ypf/resumen.texto: In April 2012 the government took control of YPF, and in May Congress approved, by a wide majority, the expropriation of Repsol's 51% stake.

hechos/memorandum-hecho/titulo.texto: Signing of the Memorandum with Iran

hechos/memorandum-hecho/resumen.texto: On 27 January 2013 the foreign ministers of Argentina and Iran signed in Addis Ababa an agreement on the AMIA case that Iran never ratified.

hechos/eleccion-del-papa-francisco/resum.texto: On 13 March 2013 the conclave elected the Archbishop of Buenos Aires, Jorge Mario Bergoglio, as pope; he took the name Francis and was the first pope from the Americas and the first Jesuit pope.

hechos/fallo-clarin-hecho/titulo.texto: The Supreme Court upholds the Media Law

hechos/fallo-clarin-hecho/lugar.texto: Palacio de Justicia de la Nación (Tribunales)

hechos/fallo-clarin-hecho/resumen.texto: On 29 October 2013 the Court rejected Grupo Clarín's challenge to the licence limits of the Ley de Servicios de Comunicación Audiovisual.

hechos/arsat-1/resumen.texto: On 16 October 2014 ARSAT-1, the first geostationary telecommunications satellite built in Argentina, by INVAP, was launched from French Guiana.

hechos/muerte-de-nisman/lugar.texto: Le Parc Towers, Puerto Madero, Buenos Aires

hechos/muerte-de-nisman/resumen.texto: On 18 January 2015 Nisman was found dead from a gunshot in his apartment in Puerto Madero. The first forensic examinations found no trace of third parties; a 2017 Gendarmería report concluded that he was murdered, and in 2018 the Federal Court of Appeals provisionally deemed the homicide proven. As of 2026 there had been no trial.

hechos/eleccion-de-macri/resumen.texto: On 22 November 2015, in the first presidential runoff in Argentine history, Mauricio Macri defeated Daniel Scioli with 51% of the vote.

hechos/bolsos-de-jose-lopez/resumen.texto: On 14 June 2016 police arrested former Public Works Secretary José López as he was throwing bags containing almost nine million dollars into a convent in General Rodríguez.

hechos/megacausa-esma/resumen.texto: On 29 November 2017 Federal Oral Court 5 convicted 48 defendants, 29 of them to life imprisonment, for the crimes committed at the ESMA, including the death flights.

hechos/ara-san-juan/titulo.texto: Sinking of the submarine ARA San Juan

hechos/ara-san-juan/resumen.texto: On 15 November 2017 the Navy submarine ARA San Juan disappeared in the South Atlantic with its 44 crew members; it was found at a depth of about 900 metres in November 2018.

hechos/acuerdo-con-el-fmi-de-2018/resume.texto: After a run on the peso, the Macri government signed a stand-by agreement with the IMF in June 2018, expanded in September to some 57 billion dollars, the largest in the institution's history.

hechos/causa-cuadernos/resumen.texto: On 1 August 2018 the arrests of former officials and businessmen ordered by Judge Bonadio on the basis of the notebooks of driver Oscar Centeno became public; dozens of businessmen testified as cooperating witnesses.

hechos/condena-de-boudou/titulo.texto: Conviction of Boudou in the Ciccone case

hechos/condena-de-boudou/resumen.texto: On 7 August 2018 Federal Oral Court 4 sentenced former vice president Amado Boudou to five years and ten months in prison; the conviction became final in December 2020.

hechos/condena-de-de-vido/titulo.texto: Conviction of De Vido for the Once tragedy

hechos/condena-de-de-vido/resumen.texto: On 10 October 2018 Federal Oral Court 4 sentenced former minister Julio De Vido to five years and eight months in prison for fraudulent administration; the Supreme Court upheld the conviction in November 2025 and De Vido was taken into custody.

hechos/condena-de-milagro-sala/resumen.texto: In January 2019 a court in Jujuy sentenced Milagro Sala to thirteen years in prison in the Pibes Villeros case; the combined sentence of fifteen years became final in 2025.

hechos/condena-de-jose-lopez/titulo.texto: Conviction of José López for illicit enrichment

hechos/condena-de-jose-lopez/resumen.texto: On 12 June 2019 Federal Oral Court 1 sentenced José López to six years in prison for illicit enrichment over the money in the bags.

hechos/eleccion-de-alberto-fernandez/res.texto: On 27 October 2019 the Frente de Todos ticket of Alberto Fernández and Cristina Kirchner defeated Macri in the first round with 48% of the vote.

hechos/pandemia-de-covid-19/resumen.texto: From 20 March 2020 a mandatory lockdown was in force that lasted for months, one of the longest in the world; more than 130,000 people died. The revelation of a party at the Quinta de Olivos during the lockdown damaged the government of Alberto Fernández.

hechos/legalizacion-del-aborto/lugar.texto: Palace of the Argentine National Congress

hechos/legalizacion-del-aborto/resumen.texto: On 30 December 2020 the Senate approved the voluntary termination of pregnancy, while thousands of demonstrators with green and sky-blue scarves waited outside Congress.

hechos/sobreseimiento-dolar-futuro/titul.texto: Dismissal in the dollar futures case

hechos/sobreseimiento-dolar-futuro/resum.texto: On 13 April 2021 the Court of Cassation dismissed the charges against Cristina Kirchner, Axel Kicillof and the other defendants in the case over the sale of dollar futures, finding that no crime had been committed.

hechos/condena-de-lazaro-baez/titulo.texto: Conviction of Lázaro Báez in the K money trail case

hechos/condena-de-lazaro-baez/resumen.texto: On 24 February 2021 Federal Oral Court 4 sentenced Lázaro Báez to twelve years in prison for money laundering; the Court of Cassation upheld the conviction in 2023 and reduced the sentence to ten years.

hechos/sobreseimientos-de-2021/titulo.texto: Dismissals in the Memorandum and Hotesur-Los Sauces cases

hechos/sobreseimientos-de-2021/resumen.texto: In October and November 2021 two oral courts dismissed the charges against Cristina Kirchner before trial in the Memorandum with Iran case and in the Hotesur-Los Sauces case.

hechos/revocacion-de-sobreseimientos/tit.texto: Court of Cassation overturns the Memorandum and Hotesur dismissals

hechos/revocacion-de-sobreseimientos/res.texto: In September 2023 the Court of Cassation overturned the 2021 dismissals and ordered Cristina Kirchner to stand trial in both cases; in December 2024 the Supreme Court confirmed that she must stand trial in the Memorandum case.

hechos/intento-de-asesinato-de-cfk/resum.texto: On 1 September 2022 Fernando Sabag Montiel pointed a pistol at the vice president's head outside her home in Recoleta and pulled the trigger twice, but the gun did not fire; he was arrested on the spot.

hechos/condena-vialidad/titulo.texto: Conviction of Cristina Kirchner in the Vialidad case

hechos/condena-vialidad/resumen.texto: On 6 December 2022 Federal Oral Court 2 sentenced Vice President Cristina Kirchner to six years in prison and a lifetime ban from public office for fraudulent administration in public works in Santa Cruz; she denounced “lawfare”.

hechos/eleccion-de-milei/resumen.texto: On 19 November 2023 Javier Milei defeated Sergio Massa in the runoff with almost 56% of the vote; he took office on 10 December.

hechos/ley-bases-sancion/lugar.texto: Palace of the Argentine National Congress

hechos/ley-bases-sancion/resumen.texto: On 27 June 2024 the Chamber of Deputies approved the final version of the Ley Bases, the first major legislative package of the Milei government, which the Senate had passed with the tie-breaking vote of Vice President Villarruel.

hechos/juicio-por-el-intento-de-asesinat.texto: Trial for the attempted assassination of Cristina Kirchner
The trial before Federal Oral Court 6 began on 26 June 2024 and ended on 8 October 2025 with Fernando Sabag Montiel sentenced to ten years in prison.

hechos/confirmacion-vialidad-casacion/ti.texto: The Court of Cassation upholds the Vialidad conviction

hechos/confirmacion-vialidad-casacion/re.texto: On 13 November 2024 Chamber IV of the Court of Cassation upheld Cristina Kirchner's conviction and refused to add the charge of criminal association.

hechos/vialidad-corte-suprema/titulo.texto: The Supreme Court makes Cristina Kirchner's conviction final

hechos/vialidad-corte-suprema/lugar.texto: Palacio de Justicia de la Nación (Tribunales)

hechos/vialidad-corte-suprema/resumen.texto: On 10 June 2025 the Supreme Court made the Vialidad conviction final; Cristina Kirchner was placed under house arrest at her home on San José street, and thousands of supporters rallied in her support.

hechos/caso-libra/resumen.texto: On 14 February 2025 Milei promoted the cryptocurrency $LIBRA on his social media; it rose and collapsed within hours, causing losses for thousands of buyers. Criminal complaints were filed and Congress set up an investigative committee; on 23 October 2026 Judge Marcelo Martínez de Giorgi dismissed the charges against Milei and ten other people under investigation at the request of prosecutor Eduardo Taiano, who found no evidence of a crime; plaintiffs who had been removed from the case challenged the decision.

hechos/muerte-del-papa-francisco/resumen.texto: Francis died in the Vatican on 21 April 2025, Easter Monday; on 8 May the conclave elected the American Robert Prevost, Leo XIV, as his successor.

hechos/elecciones-legislativas-de-2025/r.texto: On 26 October 2025, in the first national elections held with a single paper ballot, La Libertad Avanza was the most-voted party nationwide, after losing the Buenos Aires provincial elections to the Peronists in September.

hechos/juicio-de-los-cuadernos/titulo.texto: Oral trial in the Notebooks case

hechos/juicio-de-los-cuadernos/resumen.texto: On 6 November 2025 the trial of Cristina Kirchner, Julio De Vido and dozens of former officials and businessmen began before Federal Oral Court 7, broadcast live; beforehand, the court had rejected offers of money from several defendants to close the case.

hechos/juicio-por-ypf/titulo.texto: Trial over the expropriation of YPF in New York

hechos/juicio-por-ypf/lugar.texto: Daniel Patrick Moynihan Courthouse, New York

hechos/juicio-por-ypf/resumen.texto: Minority shareholders of YPF, financed by the Burford fund, sued Argentina; in 2023 Judge Loretta Preska ordered the country to pay some 16 billion dollars and in 2025 ordered it to hand over its YPF shares, but in 2026 the Court of Appeals reversed the judgment.

lugares/plaza-de-mayo/resumen.texto: Founding square of Buenos Aires, facing the Casa Rosada and the Cabildo. It was the scene of 17 October 1945, the bombing of 16 June 1955, the marches of the Mothers from 1977 onwards and the protests of December 2001.

lugares/piramide-de-mayo/resumen.texto: The first national monument, erected in 1811 in the centre of the Plaza de Mayo. Since 1977 the Mothers of Plaza de Mayo have marched around it every Thursday, and their headscarves are painted on the ground of the square.

lugares/cabildo-de-buenos-aires/resumen.texto: Seat of the colonial municipal government, built in its present form in the 18th century and scene of the May Revolution of 1810; it lost arches in 1889 and 1931 when avenues were opened.

lugares/casa-rosada/resumen.texto: Seat of the national executive, facing the Plaza de Mayo, completed in 1898 on the site of the old fort. Perón and Eva Perón spoke from its balcony, and in 1955 it was a target of the bombing of the Plaza de Mayo.

lugares/congreso-de-la-nacion-argentina/.texto: Palace of the Argentine National Congress

Seat of the legislature, inaugurated in 1906 facing the Plaza de los Dos Congresos. The Sáenz Peña Law, women's suffrage and convertibility were voted there, and the large demonstrations over Resolution 125, same-sex marriage, legal abortion and the Ley Bases gathered in front of it.

lugares/palacio-de-justicia-buenos-aires.texto: Palacio de Justicia de la Nación (Tribunales)

Seat of the Supreme Court of Justice of the Nation, facing Plaza Lavalle, inaugurated in 1942. The Trial of the Juntas (1985) was held in its courtroom, and there the Court issued the Simón (2005) and Clarín (2013) rulings and the confirmation of the Vialidad conviction (2025).

lugares/comodoro-py/resumen.texto: Building at Avenida Comodoro Py 2002, in Retiro, built for Vialidad Nacional and occupied since the 1990s by the federal criminal courts and oral courts. The Vialidad, Notebooks, Hotesur and Memorandum cases and the trial for the attempted assassination of Cristina Kirchner were investigated and tried there.

lugares/quinta-de-olivos/resumen.texto: Official residence of the President of the Nation, in Olivos, north of Buenos Aires. Perón died there in 1974, and the Olivos Pact between Menem and Alfonsín was signed there in 1993.

lugares/cementerio-de-la-recoleta/resume.texto: The first public cemetery in Buenos Aires. It holds the tombs of Sarmiento, Alem, Yrigoyen, Alfonsín and, in the Duarte family vault, Eva Perón.

lugares/casa-de-tucuman/resumen.texto: House in San Miguel de Tucumán where independence was declared in 1816. Perón chose the same place and the same date, 9 July 1947, to sign the Declaration of Economic Independence.

lugares/isla-martin-garcia/resumen.texto: Island in the Río de la Plata opposite the mouth of the Uruguay, disputed since the colonial period. Brown’s squadron took it in 1814, and in the 1870s and 1880s it was a place of confinement for Indigenous prisoners from the frontier campaigns. In the 20th century Yrigoyen (1930), Perón (October 1945) and Frondizi (1962) were imprisoned there.

lugares/penal-de-ushuaia/resumen.texto: Prison for repeat offenders and political prisoners in Tierra del Fuego, built by the inmates themselves from 1902 and closed in 1947. Simón Radowitzky was held there between 1911 and 1930; it is now a museum.

lugares/universidad-de-buenos-aires/resu.texto: It was inaugurated on August 12, 1821, during the government of Martín Rodríguez, with Antonio Sáenz as its first rector. It is the largest university in the country, public and free of tuition since 1949. In 1966 the Night of the Long Batons (Noche de los Bastones Largos) forcibly cleared its faculties, and four of Argentina’s Nobel laureates came from it.

lugares/universidad-nacional-de-cordoba/.texto: It grew out of the Jesuits’ Colegio Máximo in Córdoba. In 1613 Bishop Trejo committed his property to found it, and the papal brief of 1621 and the royal decree (real cédula) of 1622 authorized it to confer degrees. It is the oldest university in the country. In 1918 its students launched the University Reform, which proclaimed autonomy and co-government and spread across Latin America.

lugares/esma/resumen.texto: Navy Mechanics School in Núñez, where the largest clandestine detention centre of the dictatorship operated between 1976 and 1983; some five thousand people passed through it. Since 2004 it has been the Espacio Memoria, and in 2023 UNESCO declared its museum a World Heritage Site.

lugares/la-perla/resumen.texto: Clandestine detention centre of the Third Army Corps on the outskirts of Córdoba, through which more than two thousand people passed. It is now an Espacio para la Memoria; its mega-trial ended in 2016 with 28 life sentences.

lugares/campo-de-mayo/resumen.texto: The Army's largest garrison, northwest of Buenos Aires. During the dictatorship it housed clandestine centres, such as El Campito, and a clandestine maternity ward where babies of detained women were appropriated.

lugares/automotores-orletti/resumen.texto: Garage in the Floresta neighbourhood used between May and November 1976 as an Operation Condor clandestine centre, where Uruguayan, Chilean, Bolivian and Cuban prisoners were held.

lugares/estacion-once/resumen.texto: Terminus of the Sarmiento line in Balvanera. On 22 February 2012 a train crashed into the platform's buffer stop and 52 people died; the tragedy led to the conviction of businessmen and officials, among them Ricardo Jaime and Julio De Vido.

lugares/islas-malvinas/resumen.texto: Archipelago in the South Atlantic occupied by the United Kingdom since 1833 and claimed by Argentina. The UN regards it as a decolonization case and called for negotiations (Resolution 2065, 1965); in 1982 it was the scene of the war, and in 2013 its inhabitants voted to remain a British territory.

lugares/puerto-argentino/resumen.texto: Capital and port of the Falkland (Malvinas) Islands. It was occupied by Argentine forces on 2 April 1982, and General Mario Benjamín Menéndez surrendered there on 14 June.

lugares/isla-huemul/resumen.texto: Island in Lake Nahuel Huapi, off Bariloche, where Ronald Richter set up the laboratories of the Huemul Project for nuclear fusion between 1949 and 1952.

lugares/instituto-balseiro/resumen.texto: Institute of physics and nuclear engineering at the Centro Atómico Bariloche, created in 1955 by the Comisión Nacional de Energía Atómica and the Universidad de Cuyo and directed in its early years by José Antonio Balseiro.

lugares/invap/resumen.texto: Technology company of the province of Río Negro, headquartered in Bariloche, founded in 1976. It built research nuclear reactors sold to several countries and the ARSAT geostationary satellites.
